title: Computer Science, Linux, Networking, and Engineering Foundations
purpose: Trace a program from the machine to the shell and follow a request from client to server.
why: Trace a program from the machine to the shell and follow a request from client to server.
outcomes: Identify a broken ownership check and a logging mistake in a basic service diagram.
The test table denies cross-user access and shows that an identifier can be logged without logging the credential.

topics.title: Introduction to Computer Science and Software Engineering
topics.description: A word-counting tool turns a file into an integer. Its input is bytes, the program supplies the instructions and the count is the output. Write a contract for a word counter. For an empty file and a three-word file, record the inputs, outputs and one failure a test should catch.

subtopics.title: Introduction to Computer Science and Software Engineering · worked exercise

topics.title: How a Computer Executes Instructions
topics.description: Adding 2 and 3 requires reading operands, executing an addition and placing the result where the next instruction can read it. Draw the instruction and data flow for reading two integers, adding them and printing 5. Mark what runs on the CPU and when input or output must wait.

subtopics.title: How a Computer Executes Instructions · worked exercise

topics.title: CPU, Cores, RAM, Storage, and Memory Basics
topics.description: Saving a model puts bytes on disk. Loading those bytes for computation consumes RAM, even if the original file still exists on disk. Inspect CPU count, available RAM and storage for your machine. Explain whether a task that needs 4 GB of RAM can be evaluated using disk space alone.

subtopics.title: CPU, Cores, RAM, Storage, and Memory Basics · worked exercise

topics.title: Bits, Bytes, Binary, and Data Representation (one focused practical topic; do not over-expand digital logic)
topics.description: The bit pattern 00001101 represents 13 as an unsigned integer because its active weights are 8, 4 and 1. Encode 13 and 255 in eight bits, decode 00101010, then state the smallest byte count needed for an unsigned value of 256.

subtopics.title: Binary, Bits, Bytes, and Data Representation · worked exercise

topics.title: Operating System Fundamentals
topics.description: An ordinary program asks the operating system to open a file. The kernel checks permissions and returns a handle or an error. Draw the application-to-kernel boundary for opening a protected file. Use a disposable file to observe a successful read and explain where a permission denial would occur.

topics.title: Processes, Threads, and Basic Scheduling Concepts
topics.description: A process waiting for disk input is blocked. The scheduler can run a different ready task during the wait. Draw the ready, running and waiting states for two tasks, one with a disk wait. Identify shared data that two threads would need to protect.

subtopics.title: Processes, Threads, and Basic Scheduling · worked exercise

topics.title: Filesystems, Paths, Environment Variables, and Process Environment
topics.description: The relative path config/settings.json is resolved from the working directory, while an absolute path begins at a filesystem root. In a disposable directory, read the same fixture using a relative path and an absolute path. Run a child shell with a harmless example variable and check its value.

subtopics.title: Filesystems, Paths, and Environment Variables · worked exercise

topics.title: Command-Line Fundamentals: pwd, ls, cd, cat, less, mkdir, cp, mv, and rm safely
topics.description: A terminal displays input and output. A shell interprets commands, resolves paths and invokes programs. Create a scratch directory with one nested folder. From two working directories, show how to reach the same file using relative paths and verify each location with pwd.

subtopics.title: Command Line and Terminal Fundamentals · worked exercise

topics.title: Linux Fundamentals and the Linux Filesystem
topics.description: A distribution's package manager tracks files and dependencies installed through that distribution's package system. In a disposable Linux environment, identify the distribution and inspect the package manager's metadata for an installed tool. Record the command and version without modifying the system.

topics.title: Linux Permissions, Ownership, Users, and Groups
topics.description: A readable file in a directory that you cannot traverse can still be unreachable by its path. File and directory permissions answer different questions. In an owned scratch directory, inspect user and group ownership and predict which test access would fail after changing only directory traversal permissions. Restore the directory afterward.

subtopics.title: Create, copy, move, and delete operations
Linux Files, Directories, Permissions, and Ownership · worked exercise

topics.title: Linux Processes, Services, Signals, and Resource Inspection
topics.description: A process can be running while its service is unhealthy. A log or health response gives evidence about behavior beyond the process ID. Start a harmless local process, find its PID and inspect CPU and memory information. Stop only that process and record how you verified it exited.

subtopics.title: Linux Processes, Services, and Resource Inspection · worked exercise

topics.title: Linux Text Processing and Search: grep, find, pipes, redirection, and exit codes
topics.description: A pipe sends one command's standard output to another command's standard input. For a small fixture, grep ERROR app.log writes matching lines, while redirecting stdout with > creates or truncates the named output file. Use a separate scratch output path so the input stays intact.

subtopics.title: Linux Text Processing and Search: grep, find, pipes, redirection, and exit codes

topics.title: Bash Shell Scripting: variables, arguments, conditions, loops, functions, and safe script execution
topics.description: A command that accepts a file path needs quoting so a path such as sample data.txt is passed as one argument. Write a Bash script that counts lines in a supplied file, including a fixture with a space in its name. Check its output and its exit code when the path is absent.

subtopics.title: Shell Commands and Basic Bash Scripting · worked exercise

topics.title: Practical Linux Troubleshooting Commands: ps, top/htop, ss, lsof, curl, journalctl, df, du, and free. Teach ss as the modern first choice for socket inspection; mention netstat only as legacy context if encountered
topics.description: A local service can have a PID while still failing to listen. ss -ltn shows listening TCP sockets and curl tests the HTTP response. A journal is useful on a systemd host when the account can read it. Use netstat only to interpret older instructions.

subtopics.title: Practical Linux Troubleshooting Commands: ps, top/htop, ss, lsof, curl, journalctl, df, du, and free. Teach ss as the modern first choice for socket inspection; mention netstat only as legacy context if encountered

topics.title: SSH, Secure Remote Access, and Basic File Transfer
topics.description: The SSH host key identifies the remote server. Your own key authenticates your user account. A fingerprint mismatch should stop a connection until you verify the new value through a trusted channel.

subtopics.title: SSH, Secure Remote Access, and Basic File Transfer

topics.title: Git Fundamentals and Version Control
topics.description: Editing a tracked file changes the working tree. Staging prepares the selected content for the next commit. Create a throwaway repository and edit two files. Stage one file and show which changes appear in the staged diff and which remain unstaged.

subtopics.title: Git Fundamentals and Version Control · worked exercise

topics.title: Git Branches, Commits, Merges, and Conflict Resolution
topics.description: Two branches can both change the same line. A merge conflict asks you to choose or combine changes before recording the result. Use a throwaway repository to create conflicting edits, resolve them deliberately and verify the final file and merge history.

subtopics.title: Git Branches, Commits, Merges, and Conflict Resolution · worked exercise

topics.title: GitHub, Pull Requests, and Code Review Basics
topics.description: A pull request gives a reviewer the proposed diff, its rationale and the checks used to verify the change. Write a draft pull-request description for the local merge. Include one behavior change, its test and one review question. Keep the exercise local.

subtopics.title: GitHub, Pull Requests, and Code Review Basics · worked exercise

topics.title: Networking Fundamentals: IP Addresses, Subnets at a basic level, Ports, DNS, and Routing Concepts
topics.description: A service on your machine can be reachable from the same machine through the loopback interface while remaining unavailable from another computer. Diagram a local client, its network address and an owned endpoint. Label what changes if the service becomes reachable over a private network.

subtopics.title: IP Addresses, Ports, DNS, TCP, and UDP · worked exercise

topics.title: TCP and UDP: what they do and when the distinction matters
topics.description: TCP presents an ordered stream of bytes. UDP sends separate datagrams and leaves recovery to the application if it needs it. A telemetry sample that arrives late can be less valuable than a newer sample.

subtopics.title: TCP and UDP: what they do and when the distinction matters

topics.title: HTTP Request/Response Lifecycle, Methods, Headers, Status Codes, and TLS/HTTPS
topics.description: A GET request for a missing record can receive 404. A network timeout yields no HTTP response to interpret. Trace one successful and one failed request to a local or owned endpoint. Label method, path, response status and whether a response body was available.

subtopics.title: Read an HTTP exchange without a browser UI
HTTPS, TLS, and Secure Communication · worked exercise

topics.title: Client-Server Architecture, REST Concepts, JSON, and Serialization
topics.description: A client requests a resource such as /models/42. The service controls data and behavior and returns a representation to the client. Draft two resource URLs and choose HTTP methods and status codes for reading an existing record, looking up a missing record and creating a new one.

subtopics.title: Client-Server Architecture and REST Concepts · worked exercise
JSON, Serialization, and Data Exchange · worked exercise

topics.title: APIs, Authentication Concepts, and API Documentation
topics.description: An API contract explains valid requests and possible responses. Authentication establishes the caller's identity. Authorization decides whether that caller can access a record. Read the documentation for an owned fixture API or draft its contract. Show how a valid request, a request missing credentials and an authenticated but unauthorized request differ.

subtopics.title: APIs, Authentication Concepts, and API Documentation · worked exercise

topics.title: Basic Web-Service Security and Engineering Practices
topics.description: A service should validate an incoming ID and check ownership before retrieving private data. A log can record a request ID and denial without including a credential. Draw the trust boundary of a toy student-record endpoint. Write acceptance cases for malformed IDs, wrong-owner requests and a log that excludes credentials.

subtopics.title: Basic Web-Service Security and Engineering Practices · worked exercise

title: Python Programming and Concurrency: Beginner to Professional
purpose: Write, test, package and maintain Python programs that handle real inputs and failures.
why: Write, test, package and maintain Python programs that handle real inputs and failures.
outcomes: Build and verify an installable small Python program independently.
The installed artifact includes the necessary files, the command works from another directory and the invalid case exits predictably.

topics.title: Python Installation and Development Setup
topics.description: A terminal may resolve python to a different installation than the editor uses. The interpreter path identifies which one actually runs the code. Record the interpreter path and version from a terminal and from the editor. Align them and run a file from both.

subtopics.title: Python Installation and Development Setup · worked exercise

topics.title: Running Python Programs and Understanding the Interpreter
topics.description: An interactive prompt evaluates input immediately. Running a script executes the instructions stored in a file. Evaluate the same arithmetic expression in the prompt and in a script. Explain why the script needs an explicit print to display the result.

subtopics.title: Running Python Programs and Understanding the Interpreter · worked exercise

topics.title: Variables, Naming, and Basic Data Types
topics.description: A variable name refers to a value. Assigning another value changes the reference, while mutating a shared list can affect multiple references. Show the types of a count, ratio and boolean. Create two names for one list and contrast mutating the list with rebinding one name.

subtopics.title: Variables, Naming, and Basic Data Types · worked exercise

topics.title: Input, Output, and Type Conversion
topics.description: Input from the terminal is text. Converting the string 12 to an integer enables arithmetic, while converting twelve raises an error. Read a count from the terminal. Demonstrate a correct conversion and record the exception you observe for nonnumeric text.

subtopics.title: Input, Output, and Type Conversion · worked exercise

topics.title: Operators and Expressions
topics.description: The operators / and // answer different questions. For positive operands, 7 / 2 gives 3.5 and 7 // 2 gives 3. Predict and run expressions with division, remainder and parentheses. Check that quotient times divisor plus remainder recovers each positive input.

topics.title: Conditional Statements
topics.description: An if/elif chain runs the first matching branch. Ordering a broad condition before a narrower one can hide the narrower case. Write a branch for empty, short and long text. Test inputs on both sides of the length boundary and at the exact boundary.

topics.title: Loops and Loop Control
topics.description: Break ends the nearest loop. Continue skips the rest of the current iteration and proceeds to the next one. Scan a list of text records, skip blank lines and stop at an explicit sentinel. Record the number of processed rows for a fixture with both cases.

subtopics.title: Loops and Loop Control · worked exercise

topics.title: Strings and String Operations
topics.description: String operations return new values. Calling strip without keeping its return value leaves the original text unchanged. Normalize a username by trimming and case-folding. Check whitespace-only input and demonstrate that the original value is unchanged.

subtopics.title: Strings and String Operations · worked exercise

topics.title: Lists and List Operations
topics.description: A list keeps order and duplicates. Its first item is at index zero. A slice produces a new list of the selected items. Process a list of recent request IDs. Add one, keep the last three, and verify behavior for an empty input list.

subtopics.title: Lists and List Operations · worked exercise

topics.title: Tuples and Sets
topics.description: A tuple can represent a fixed pair. A set represents unique values and does not promise an application-level display order. Represent each input as a pair of account and record IDs. Deduplicate repeated pairs and compare set membership with the original list.

topics.title: Dictionaries and Nested Data
topics.description: A dictionary associates a key with a value. A nested result can carry separate usage and request data, and a missing field needs a deliberate default or error. Create two synthetic request dictionaries, one without token usage. Extract the count using an explicit missing-data rule and verify both outputs.

subtopics.title: Dictionaries and Nested Data · worked exercise

topics.title: Functions and Reusable Code
topics.description: A function can return a result for its caller to test or reuse. Printing a value displays it without returning it. Extract the string normalization step into a function. Check the returned values for two fixtures and call the same function from two places.

subtopics.title: Functions and Reusable Code · worked exercise

topics.title: Parameters, Arguments, Return Values, Scope, and Mutability
topics.description: A parameter name exists inside the function. A caller can supply a value positionally or by its declared keyword when the signature allows it. Design a signature for a summary function with a default limit. Compare omitted, positional and keyword arguments and show which local names are unavailable outside it.

subtopics.title: Parameters, Arguments, Return Values, and Scope · worked exercise

topics.title: Lambda Functions and Functional Basics (short practical lesson)
topics.description: A small key function can sort rows by a chosen field without altering those rows. Sort three records by their duration with a lambda key. Test an equal-duration tie and explain the order.

subtopics.title: Lambda Functions and Functional Basics · worked exercise

topics.title: List, Dictionary, and Set Comprehensions (teach together with simple examples)
topics.description: The same input can produce a list of normalized names, a dictionary indexed by ID, or a set of unique names. The result types preserve different information. Build all three results from four fixture rows with a repeated name. Compare each result with an equivalent explicit loop.

subtopics.title: List, Dictionary, and Set Comprehensions · worked exercise

topics.title: Modules, Imports, and Packages
topics.description: An import executes module-level code on first load in a process. Putting CLI behavior behind an entry point keeps the imported helper usable in tests. Move a helper into a module. Import it from a second file and prove it does not print or read files just because it was imported.

subtopics.title: Modules, Imports, and Packages · worked exercise

topics.title: Project Structure and the Python Module System
topics.description: A CLI module can handle input and output while a separate processing module receives ordinary values and returns testable results. Split a two-operation script into entry, processing and test modules. Run it as a module and show a test that uses the processing function directly.

subtopics.title: Project Structure and the Python Module System · worked exercise

topics.title: File Handling and pathlib
topics.description: A pathlib Path represents a filesystem location. Opening the same relative path from another working directory can resolve to a different file. Read and copy a UTF-8 fixture using pathlib in a scratch directory. Test a missing file and avoid overwriting an existing output.

subtopics.title: File Handling and pathlib · worked exercise

topics.title: Working with JSON, CSV, and Common Data Formats
topics.description: CSV can quote commas inside a field. JSON preserves nested values. Manual splitting and concatenation can corrupt those cases. Parse a CSV row containing a quoted comma, convert it to JSON, then check the parsed values after reading it back.

subtopics.title: Working with JSON, CSV, and Common Data Formats · worked exercise

topics.title: Exception Handling and Custom Exceptions
topics.description: An exception can distinguish invalid application input from an unavailable file. A caller can handle each failure differently. Raise a named invalid-record error in a parser. Write fixtures for missing files and invalid records and show that their error paths stay distinct.

subtopics.title: Exception Handling and Custom Exceptions · worked exercise

topics.title: Object-Oriented Programming
topics.description: An object can group a state and the operations that keep that state valid, such as a counter that never goes below zero. Describe the public operations and invariants of a quota counter. Trace two valid calls and one request that violates the invariant.

topics.title: Classes, Objects, Attributes, and Methods
topics.description: Each instance can hold a different count. A mutable class attribute is shared, which can accidentally mix state between instances. Create two counters, update only one and verify their state stays separate. Explain how a shared mutable class attribute would change the result.

subtopics.title: Classes, Objects, Attributes, and Methods · worked exercise

topics.title: Encapsulation, Inheritance, and Polymorphism
topics.description: A caller can use two implementations through a common operation. Each implementation can handle the operation differently while preserving its contract. Implement two small report sinks with the same write contract. Pass each to the same caller and verify it does not need to inspect the concrete class.

subtopics.title: Encapsulation, Inheritance, and Polymorphism · worked exercise

topics.title: Abstraction and Composition
topics.description: A service that receives a storage component can change storage independently of the service’s input and output contract. Pass an in-memory store into a record service. Verify the service's tests can replace storage without rewriting the class hierarchy.

topics.title: Dataclasses and Practical Object Modeling
topics.description: A dataclass can represent one parsed record with named fields. A type annotation describes intended values, but it does not validate arbitrary input at runtime. Create a dataclass for a usage event, then validate raw count and event ID before constructing it. Compare two events by value.

subtopics.title: Dataclasses and Practical Object Modeling · worked exercise

topics.title: Iterators and Generators (practical use in memory-efficient processing)
topics.description: A generator produces values when the caller requests them. Once exhausted, it does not start over automatically. Generate records from a small fixture lazily. Consume the first two records, inspect what remains, then show how to start a new generator.

topics.title: Decorators (understand and write a simple decorator; do not over-focus on metaprogramming)
topics.description: A decorator can add timing to a function while forwarding its arguments and return value. Wrap a pure function with a decorator that records invocation. Verify its return value and exception behavior stay the same.

topics.title: Context Managers and with (understand resource cleanup and write a simple context manager only after using built-in ones)
topics.description: A context manager handles setup and cleanup. Leaving a with block due to an exception still calls its exit behavior. Open a scratch file inside a with block, raise a controlled exception and verify the handle is closed in the exception handler.

topics.title: Type Hints and Typed Interfaces
topics.description: A list of integers and a list of strings can have the same runtime container class. Type hints document the expected element type for a checker. Annotate a parser and its return type. Run a checker on a valid call and a mismatched call, then explain what needs separate runtime validation.

subtopics.title: Type Hints and Typed Interfaces · worked exercise

topics.title: Virtual Environments and Dependency Management
topics.description: A virtual environment has its own dependency installation directory. It lets two projects use different compatible versions without changing the system interpreter's packages. Create a fresh virtual environment, record the interpreter and package paths, and show how to verify the environment is active.

subtopics.title: Virtual Environments and Dependency Management · worked exercise

topics.title: Package Installation, Locking, and Reproducible Environments
topics.description: A dependency record helps another environment select the versions used in a test. A fresh install is evidence that the list is complete. Install a single test dependency in a disposable environment and record the version. Recreate the environment from the recorded requirements and run a smoke test.

subtopics.title: Package Installation and Reproducible Environments · worked exercise

topics.title: Logging and Debugging
topics.description: A log can show that parsing failed for request R, while a debugger shows the local value that reached the failing line. Neither needs to record private request data. Reproduce a malformed fixture, step through the failure and add a log with a correlation ID and safe error category. Check that the raw fixture is absent from the log.

topics.title: Unit Testing with pytest
topics.description: A fixture prepares repeatable input. An assertion verifies the result. A deliberate failing case confirms the test actually runs and catches the change. Test the parser for valid, missing and malformed values using pytest. Change one expected result to observe a failure, then restore the expectation.

subtopics.title: Unit Testing with pytest · worked exercise

topics.title: Synchronous vs Asynchronous Programming: when each model is appropriate
topics.description: Await lets another task proceed while the current task waits. Calling blocking work inside the event loop can still delay every task. Compare two waiting tasks run one after the other with the same tasks scheduled together. Record elapsed time and show the effect of a blocking wait.

topics.title: async/await, coroutines, and the asyncio event loop
topics.description: Calling an async function creates a coroutine object. asyncio.run starts a top-level event loop for a script, and awaiting the coroutine lets it run. A coroutine that awaits a timer yields execution so another runnable task can make progress.

subtopics.title: async/await, coroutines, and the asyncio event loop

topics.title: Tasks, task groups where supported, gather, and concurrent I/O workflows
topics.description: A task schedules a coroutine on the current event loop. gather can return results in argument order even when they finish differently. In a TaskGroup, a failing task causes unfinished siblings to be cancelled and awaited before the failure is reported.

subtopics.title: Tasks, task groups where supported, gather, and concurrent I/O workflows

topics.title: Async timeouts, cancellation, semaphores, and bounded concurrency
topics.description: A semaphore limits how many operations enter a protected section at once. A timeout can cancel the active operation, so resource release belongs in an async context manager or finally block.

subtopics.title: Async timeouts, cancellation, semaphores, and bounded concurrency

topics.title: Async HTTP requests and safe concurrent calls to external APIs
topics.description: Opening a new client for every call loses the opportunity to reuse pooled connections. Reusing one client with explicit timeouts lets independent I/O overlap while the semaphore protects the downstream service.

subtopics.title: Async HTTP requests and safe concurrent calls to external APIs

topics.title: Async context managers and asynchronous resource cleanup
topics.description: An asynchronous context manager can await setup and cleanup. async with calls its exit method when the body returns or raises, so a client can release network resources in either case.

subtopics.title: Async context managers and asynchronous resource cleanup

topics.title: Threads, thread pools, and asyncio.to_thread for blocking I/O
topics.description: A synchronous blocking call inside an async function occupies the event-loop thread. asyncio.to_thread runs the callable in a worker thread so the loop can continue handling other waiting tasks.

subtopics.title: Threads, thread pools, and asyncio.to_thread for blocking I/O

topics.title: Multiprocessing and process pools for CPU-bound work
topics.description: A process pool uses separate Python processes. Work and results cross a process boundary, so sending a tiny task may cost more than computing it directly. The main guard matters on systems that start fresh worker interpreters.

subtopics.title: Multiprocessing and process pools for CPU-bound work

topics.title: I/O-bound vs CPU-bound workloads, the GIL at a practical level, and choosing async vs threads vs processes
topics.description: Many common CPython builds use a global interpreter lock that limits parallel execution of Python bytecode in threads. Threads can still help overlap blocking I/O. A process pool can run separate Python computations at the cost of starting workers and transferring data.

subtopics.title: I/O-bound vs CPU-bound workloads, the GIL at a practical level, and choosing async vs threads vs processes

topics.title: Race Conditions, Locks, Shared State, and Thread-Safety Fundamentals
topics.description: If two threads read the same counter before either writes it, both can compute the same next value. A lock around the full read-and-write operation prevents that interleaving.

subtopics.title: Race Conditions, Locks, Shared State, and Thread-Safety Fundamentals

topics.title: Blocking-call mistakes in async applications and how to detect/fix them
topics.description: Marking a function async does not make its body nonblocking. A synchronous sleep or filesystem operation can delay unrelated tasks on the loop. A periodic heartbeat is one way to observe that delay.

subtopics.title: Blocking-call mistakes in async applications and how to detect/fix them

topics.title: Backpressure, concurrency limits, and protecting external APIs from overload
topics.description: A concurrency limit controls active work. It does not automatically limit how many tasks wait. A bounded queue applies backpressure by making a fast producer wait or deliberately reject excess work.

subtopics.title: Backpressure, concurrency limits, and protecting external APIs from overload

topics.title: Code Quality, Refactoring, and Reusable Components
topics.description: A refactor changes structure while preserving verified behavior. Keeping parsing and transformation separate lets a test focus on either part. Refactor one long fixture parser into three named steps. Run the same tests before and after, and record the behavior those tests actually protect.

subtopics.title: Code Quality, Refactoring, and Reusable Components · worked exercise

topics.title: Building and Packaging a Small Python Application
topics.description: A built distribution carries the files and metadata that an installer needs. A source checkout can mask missing package files. Build a distribution from the toolkit, install it in a clean virtual environment and run its documented entry point on a valid and malformed fixture.

subtopics.title: Package and test a Python CLI

title: Data Structures, Algorithms, and Software Engineering
purpose: Choose representations and algorithms, measure their cost and verify behavior through tests.
why: Choose representations and algorithms, measure their cost and verify behavior through tests.
outcomes: Use a minimal reproduction and basic timing evidence to distinguish symptoms from cause.
Capture the failing input, the implicated operation and the check used after the fix.

topics.title: Computational and Algorithmic Thinking
topics.description: A rule that selects overdue invoices needs inputs, a decision and an output. Define how missing dates are handled before writing a loop. Specify inputs, outputs and two edge cases for finding the oldest unprocessed job. Run the rules by hand against a five-row fixture.

subtopics.title: Computational and Algorithmic Thinking · worked exercise

topics.title: Problem Decomposition and Pseudocode
topics.description: A report job can be decomposed into parse, validate, aggregate and format. Each stage exposes an input and an output you can test. Write pseudocode for the report and a truth table for accepting a row only if its tenant and ID are valid. Trace one rejected row.

subtopics.title: Problem Decomposition and Pseudocode · worked exercise

topics.title: Time Complexity and Space Complexity
topics.description: Scanning an array once takes work that grows with its length. Making a copy during the scan adds memory that also grows with length. Count comparisons and additional stored items for scanning and copying arrays of lengths 5, 10 and 20. Separate input storage from additional storage.

subtopics.title: Measure the cost of finding a record

topics.title: Big O Notation
topics.description: A loop with 2n + 3 operations grows at the same asymptotic rate as n. A pair of nested n-step loops grows quadratically. Compare n and n squared at n=4, 8 and 16. Describe what doubling the input does and distinguish asymptotic growth from measured runtime.

topics.title: Arrays and Strings
topics.description: Access by position is fast in an array. Inserting at its beginning can require shifting later elements. Python strings do not allow in-place character updates. Trace inserting one element into the middle of a five-item array. Count shifts and compare building text in pieces with repeated concatenation in a small run.

topics.title: Hash Tables and Dictionaries
topics.description: A hash lookup identifies candidate storage locations. Different keys can collide, so the table must still check equality. Index jobs by ID and demonstrate how a duplicate ID differs from two distinct IDs. Record the cost of building the index before repeated lookups.

subtopics.title: Hash Tables and Dictionaries · worked exercise

topics.title: Linked Lists
topics.description: A linked node stores data and a reference to the next node. With a pointer to the previous node, insertion changes links without shifting a whole array. Trace inserting and removing a middle node. Test operations on an empty list and a one-node list, and explain why position lookup still traverses.

topics.title: Stacks and Queues
topics.description: A stack returns the most recent item first. A queue returns the earliest waiting item first. Feed A, B and C to both structures, then remove two items. Explain why a retry list and an undo history may need different ordering rules.

topics.title: Searching Algorithms
topics.description: Binary search discards half of a sorted interval each step. On unsorted data, discarding half can lose the target. Trace finding a target and an absent value in nine sorted IDs. State the invariant and test an empty input.

topics.title: Sorting Algorithms
topics.description: A stable sort preserves the input order of records that compare equal. That matters when one key is intentionally ordered before a second sort. Sort requests by priority and inspect equal-priority entries. Trace a simple insertion sort and count comparisons on sorted and reverse-ordered inputs.

topics.title: Recursion and Backtracking Fundamentals
topics.description: A recursive call handles a smaller state. Backtracking tries a choice, explores it and restores the state before trying the next choice. Trace all length-three binary strings with no consecutive ones. Mark the base case and show which prefixes are pruned.

subtopics.title: Recursion and Backtracking Fundamentals · worked exercise

topics.title: Trees and Binary Trees
topics.description: A rooted tree gives each non-root node one parent. A binary tree allows at most two children per node. Draw a fixture tree with a root and five nodes. Identify its leaves, height and traversal order.

subtopics.title: Trees and Binary Trees · worked exercise

topics.title: Binary Search Trees
topics.description: A search tree places smaller keys to one side and greater keys to the other. A chain-shaped tree can lose the benefit of splitting. Insert the same keys in sorted and mixed order. Compare tree heights and trace how many nodes each search visits.

topics.title: Heaps and Priority Queues

topics.description: Breadth-first search visits distance-one nodes before distance-two nodes in an unweighted graph. Depth-first search follows one branch before returning. topics.title: Choosing Data Structures for Real Problems
topics.description: A cache index needs fast key lookup, while a job scheduler needs priority ordering. One representation does not optimize both operations. topics.title: SOLID Principles at a Practical Level
topics.description: A handler depending on a small interface can use a fake store in tests and a durable store in production without needing both implementations' details. Replace a direct storage constructor with a supplied interface. Verify an unchanged contract with a fake and explain the dependency direction.

topics.title: Common Design Patterns Used in Backend Systems
topics.description: An adapter can translate a provider's response into the application's common result shape. The caller can then handle provider-specific errors consistently. subtopics.title: Common Design Patterns Used in Backend Systems · worked exercise

topics.title: Unit, Integration, and Regression Testing
topics.description: A unit test can exercise an input rule directly. An integration test verifies the rule through the service and database boundary. Build one direct parser test and one integration test for invalid records. Convert a reproduced bug into a named regression case.

subtopics.title: Unit, Integration, and Regression Testing · worked exercise

topics.title: Test Doubles, Mocking, and Dependency Isolation
topics.description: A fake provider can return a deterministic response or raise a timeout. This lets a test verify retry policy without making a network call. Inject a fake provider with a controlled first-call failure. Assert the number of calls and prove the test works with networking disabled.

subtopics.title: Test Doubles, Mocking, and Dependency Isolation · worked exercise

topics.title: Git Branching, Pull Requests, and Review Workflow in Team Projects
topics.description: A review should connect the proposed behavior, diff and verification. A passing formatting check gives different evidence from a behavioral test. Prepare a local feature branch and an example review checklist. Include one question about failure handling and respond with a test result.

subtopics.title: Git Branching, Pull Requests, and Review Workflow in Team Projects · worked exercise

topics.title: Debugging, Profiling, and Root-Cause Analysis Basics
topics.description: A slow endpoint can spend most of its time waiting on a dependency. A timing measurement across boundaries separates it from expensive application work. Reproduce a slow local fixture, time each boundary, change the suspected cause and rerun the same workload. Record evidence that could refute your hypothesis.

subtopics.title: Debugging, Profiling, and Root-Cause Analysis Basics · worked exercise

outcomes: Create a restricted database role and check its allowed and denied operations.

subtopics.title: Transactions and ACID Properties · worked exercise

subtopics.title: Data Import, Export, and Batch Processing Basics · worked exercise

topics.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
topics.description: A fitted model encodes patterns from training examples. Prediction uses that fitted state and new features. A low training error can coexist with poor generalization, so the model also needs data it has never used to fit parameters.

topics.title: Machine Learning Problem Types and Workflows
topics.description: Predicting a known urgency label is classification, while grouping unlabeled ticket text is clustering. Formulation determines the available supervision and what evaluation means. Feature values must be available at the point where the service actually predicts.

subtopics.title: Machine Learning Problem Types and Workflows

topics.title: Supervised and Unsupervised Learning
topics.description: A classifier can compare predictions to supplied targets. A clustering algorithm can group similar unlabeled records, and its usefulness depends on whether those groups are stable and meaningful for the intended workflow.

topics.title: Regression Problems and Baselines
topics.description: A constant predictor gives a reference that uses no features. The training median minimizes absolute error on the training values. A feature-based regressor should outperform a baseline for the target distribution and use case.

topics.title: Linear Regression
topics.description: Linear regression estimates the target as an intercept plus a weighted sum of features. If distance is measured in kilometers and time in minutes, its coefficient expresses the fitted change in minutes per kilometer with other inputs fixed.

topics.title: Logistic Regression
topics.description: Logistic regression maps a linear score to a number between zero and one. A threshold converts that estimate into a class decision. The boundary can move even when learned coefficients and probabilities remain fixed.

topics.title: Classification Workflows
topics.description: Classification predicts categories. A majority baseline can look strong on skewed data, so record the positive class and inspect failures by class. Stratification can help a random split preserve representative class proportions when groups or time do not dictate the split.

topics.title: Decision Trees
topics.description: A tree divides examples with feature tests, then predicts using the examples in a leaf. More splits can fit training details, including noise. A shallow tree offers fewer partitions and usually makes an individual prediction easier to inspect.

topics.title: Random Forests
topics.description: A random forest trains multiple trees on varied samples and feature subsets. Aggregating less-correlated trees can reduce variance. The aggregate may still fail when important cases are missing from training.

topics.title: Gradient Boosting Fundamentals
topics.description: Boosting builds an ensemble sequentially. In squared-error regression, a new stage can fit the residual left by the current ensemble. Learning rate controls how much of that correction is added at each stage.

topics.title: Clustering and K-Means
topics.description: K-Means alternates assigning points to their closest centroid and updating each centroid to the mean of its assigned points. The distance scale can make a large-unit feature dominate assignments.

topics.title: Feature Engineering
topics.description: Feature engineering turns raw inputs into useful model signals. For a support ticket at creation time, elapsed time since a past event may be valid. Time until the ticket is resolved is future information that would leak the outcome.

topics.title: Categorical and Numerical Feature Processing
topics.description: A column transformer routes selected columns to separate preprocessing branches. A missing numeric value and a new category represent different conditions, so each branch needs its own explicit behavior.

topics.title: Feature Scaling and Encoding
topics.description: A standard scaler stores means and scales from fitted data. A one-hot encoder stores its known category mapping. Fit both on training rows and reuse the same state so validation and production examples receive comparable inputs.

topics.title: Preprocessing Pipelines
topics.description: A preprocessing pipeline can sequence imputation and scaling. Both steps may learn state from the input. Put them behind the training fit boundary and apply transform to held-out rows with the already learned state.

topics.title: Training, Validation, and Cross-Validation
topics.description: Cross-validation repeats training and validation across folds. It only estimates the intended generalization when folds respect the relationships in the data. Repeated customers or chronological observations can make a naive random split optimistic.

topics.title: Overfitting, Underfitting, and Bias-Variance
topics.description: An inflexible model can make large errors on both training and held-out rows. An overly flexible model can fit training rows closely and still perform poorly on unseen rows. The pattern across both sets is more informative than either score alone.

topics.title: Regularization
topics.description: Ridge adds a squared coefficient penalty to the training objective. A larger penalty tends to shrink coefficients. It may reduce sensitivity to training fluctuations, though excessive shrinkage can suppress useful signal.

topics.title: Regression Evaluation Metrics
topics.description: MAE averages absolute errors. RMSE squares errors before averaging, then returns to the original units through a square root. Its larger penalty for extreme errors may matter more when a late prediction has nonlinear cost.

topics.title: Classification Evaluation Metrics
topics.description: Accuracy weights each correct row equally. A rare positive class can be missed by a high-accuracy model. Calibration asks a separate question about whether reported probability values correspond to observed frequencies.

topics.title: Confusion Matrix, Precision, Recall, and F1 Score
topics.description: Precision asks how many predicted positives were correct. Recall asks how many actual positives were found. The F1 score combines those ratios and will stay low when one of them is low.

subtopics.title: Confusion Matrix, Precision, Recall, and F1 Score

topics.title: ROC-AUC and Threshold Selection
topics.description: A binary classifier can produce scores. A threshold turns those scores into decisions. Changing the threshold changes false positives and false negatives even though the model scores stay the same.

subtopics.title: Choose a threshold with an explicit error cost

topics.title: Class Imbalance
topics.description: Class weighting changes how errors influence training. It can improve minority recall but also raise false positives. Apply mitigation inside training while keeping validation frequencies relevant to the real workload.

topics.title: Hyperparameter Tuning
topics.description: A grid enumerates its listed settings. A random search samples candidates within a budget. Each candidate must use comparable folds and preprocessing, otherwise score differences may come from the evaluation setup.

topics.title: Model Interpretability and Feature Importance
topics.description: Permutation importance measures how a fitted model's held-out score changes when a feature's values are shuffled. If another feature carries similar information, the shuffled feature may appear less important than it is to the original prediction process.

topics.title: scikit-learn Pipelines and Estimators
topics.description: A scikit-learn Pipeline fits its transformations before the estimator, then reuses them when it predicts. Parameters can be addressed by step name during model selection, so each candidate is evaluated as an entire fitted workflow.

topics.title: Model Serialization and Loading
topics.description: A serialized Python estimator may depend on the exact code and versions used to create it. Some serialization formats can execute code while loading. Treat artifacts as trusted build outputs and verify their origin before loading.

topics.title: Reproducible Experiments and Random Seeds
topics.description: A random seed controls a particular random generator. Reproducing an experiment also requires the same data revision, split policy, preprocessing and dependency versions. Use measured tolerances when exact floating-point equality is unrealistic.

topics.title: Building an End-to-End ML Pipeline
topics.description: Keep ingestion, split, fit, evaluate and artifact generation in a documented execution order. Record the training dataset and split with the artifact so the prediction service can identify the model it actually loaded.

topics.title: ML Error Analysis and Model Limitations
topics.description: An aggregate score can hide weak performance for a subgroup. Compare error rates with sample counts and inspect examples before deciding whether the problem involves labeling, missing features or a distribution shift.

subtopics.title: ML Error Analysis and Model Limitations

title: Deep Learning and Neural Networks
purpose: Trace a training step, inspect tensor shapes and train and restore a small PyTorch model.
why: Trace a training step, inspect tensor shapes and train and restore a small PyTorch model.
outcomes: Recognize which broad model architecture fits representation, generation or source-conditioned generation.
For each match, state which tokens can be attended to and whether a separate input sequence supplies context.

topics.title: Introduction to Deep Learning
topics.description: Deep learning composes trainable transformations. Intermediate activations can represent features learned from data. A neural model still needs a baseline and held-out evidence because added capacity can fit noise.

topics.title: Artificial Neurons and Perceptrons
topics.description: A perceptron forms a weighted sum of inputs plus bias, then applies a threshold. In two dimensions, inputs with zero score lie on a line that separates the two predicted regions.

topics.title: Neural Network Layers and Parameters
topics.description: A dense layer with three input features and four outputs has four weight vectors with three entries each plus four biases. Its output replaces the last feature dimension while preserving the batch dimension.

topics.title: Weights and Biases
topics.description: A weight multiplies a feature. A bias adds the same offset to every example for that neuron. With input zero, weight changes cannot alter the score, while the bias can still move it.

topics.title: Activation Functions
topics.description: ReLU replaces negative inputs with zero. Sigmoid maps each value independently into a bounded interval. Softmax normalizes several logits along a chosen axis so the entries sum to one.

topics.title: Forward Propagation
topics.description: In a forward pass, the first affine layer produces hidden scores, ReLU modifies them elementwise, and the final affine layer produces logits. Logits can be passed directly to an appropriate loss function.

topics.title: Loss Functions
topics.description: Squared error compares numeric predictions with numeric targets. Cross-entropy for mutually exclusive classes can consume raw logits and class indices. Its mean reduction combines per-example loss values for reporting or backpropagation.

topics.title: Backpropagation
topics.description: A model's forward pass produces a prediction and loss. Backpropagation populates gradients, then the optimizer updates parameters. Training loops clear old gradients before computing a new step.

topics.title: Computational Graphs and Automatic Differentiation
topics.description: A computation graph records which operations produced a value. During reverse-mode differentiation, gradient contributions flow from the loss back toward inputs. A value used in two branches receives contributions from both.

topics.title: Gradient Descent and Optimizers
topics.description: An optimizer updates parameters using gradients and possibly internal state such as running moments. Clear prior gradients when they should apply only to the current batch. Parameter values and optimizer state are distinct checkpoint concerns.

topics.title: Learning Rates and Learning-Rate Schedules
topics.description: A schedule changes the update scale over time. If a scheduler expected per epoch is called after every mini-batch, decay can happen far faster than intended. Log the applied rate beside the loss.

topics.title: Batch, Mini-Batch, and Epoch
topics.description: An epoch describes one pass over the training dataset. A mini-batch is the set processed together for an update. The last batch may be smaller when the dataset size is not divisible by the configured batch size.

topics.title: Regularization and Dropout
topics.description: Dropout randomly suppresses some activations during training and behaves differently in evaluation. Batch normalization can also switch between batch statistics and running statistics. Evaluation mode and gradient recording control different behaviors.

topics.title: PyTorch Fundamentals
topics.description: A PyTorch module owns registered parameters and can contain other modules. Calling it executes its forward behavior. Input features must match what the first layer expects, and compatible device and dtype choices matter.

topics.title: Tensors, Shapes, and Tensor Operations
topics.description: Broadcasting aligns dimensions from the right and can produce a valid but unintended operation. Label batch and feature axes, keep reduction dimensions explicit where useful and verify expected shapes before combining tensors.

topics.title: Autograd and Gradient Tracking
topics.description: A leaf tensor marked for gradient tracking can accumulate gradients after backward. A fresh forward constructs a new graph, while the leaf's gradient field can still hold previous contributions. Disable recording for pure inference when appropriate.

topics.title: Dataset and DataLoader
topics.description: A Dataset defines how to read an individual example. A DataLoader assembles examples into batches. For validation, a predictable order can help match outputs to examples even when the training order is shuffled.

topics.title: Training Loops and Validation Loops
topics.description: Training alternates forward computation, loss, backward and optimizer updates. Validation uses the same learned parameters and a held-out dataset. If the final batch has fewer examples, weighting batch means by batch size yields the correct per-example loss.

topics.title: Model Checkpoints and Reproducibility
topics.description: A training checkpoint can preserve model weights, optimizer state and progress. Reconstruct the architecture before restoring its state. Record random and data-order state where exact continuation is required.

topics.title: GPU Fundamentals for Deep Learning
topics.description: Weights, activations, gradients and optimizer state can all occupy device memory. Moving data between CPU and GPU takes time. Reduced precision can lower some allocations but requires checking operator support and training stability.

topics.title: Convolutional Neural Network Concepts
topics.description: A convolution applies a shared filter over local regions. The same weight pattern can respond to a feature at different locations. Pooling can summarize a neighborhood and reduce spatial detail.

topics.title: Recurrent Neural Network and LSTM Concepts
topics.description: A recurrent model updates hidden state step by step. Earlier information reaches later positions through that state. LSTM gates help regulate what information is retained or updated.

subtopics.title: Recurrent Neural Network and LSTM Concepts

topics.title: Attention Mechanisms
topics.description: Attention assigns weights to values based on how a query matches keys. The weighted combination changes with the query. The keys determine matching and the values supply the content being combined.

topics.title: Transformer Architecture Overview
topics.description: A transformer block typically combines attention across tokens and a feedforward operation applied to individual token representations. Residual connections carry prior representations across sublayers. Position information allows the model to distinguish token order.

topics.title: Encoder, Decoder, and Encoder-Decoder Concepts
topics.description: An encoder can build contextual representations of an input. A causal decoder generates using previous tokens. An encoder-decoder separates the source representation from the generated sequence, with cross-attention connecting them.

title: NLP, LLM Internals, and Transformer Engineering
purpose: Explain how text becomes model inputs and how transformer inference produces new tokens.
why: Explain how text becomes model inputs and how transformer inference produces new tokens.
outcomes: Recognize unsupported output and design a small test that separates known evidence from missing context.
The review identifies a fabricated or unsupported claim and provides a measurable rule for the insufficient-evidence case.

topics.title: Natural Language Processing Fundamentals
topics.description: A classifier can label a whole message. An entity extractor identifies a span within it. A sequence model can assign scores to possible next tokens. Each task needs different labels, output validation and metrics.

topics.title: Text Normalization and Preprocessing
topics.description: Lowercasing helps group words in some search systems but can erase a signal for entity recognition. Removing a common word can also change meaning when it is a negation. Compare transformations to the intended use and preserve source evidence.

topics.title: Tokenization Concepts
topics.description: Tokenization converts text into units a model can represent. Vocabulary and rules can split punctuation, whitespace and uncommon words differently. Align analysis with the tokenizer used by the model.

topics.title: Tokenizers and Subword Tokenization
topics.description: A subword vocabulary can encode an unfamiliar word as several familiar pieces. This limits vocabulary growth while keeping uncommon strings representable. The same spelling can segment differently depending on neighboring text and normalization.

topics.title: Tokens, Token IDs, and Token Counting
topics.description: The tokenizer maps each piece to an integer understood by the model. A chat template can add roles and separators. Count the actual encoded prompt and reserve space for output before making the request.

subtopics.title: Tokens, Token IDs, and Token Counting

topics.title: Word and Token Embeddings
topics.description: An embedding table maps token IDs to initial vectors. A transformer block later changes those vectors based on context. Two occurrences can start with the same lookup vector and end with different contextual representations.

topics.title: Positional Information and Positional Encoding
topics.description: Attention needs position information to distinguish sequences that contain the same tokens in different orders. A design can represent absolute position, relationships between positions or both, depending on the model.

topics.title: Self-Attention
topics.description: A transformer mixes information between token positions using attention. Queries compare with keys to produce weights over values; residual paths and normalization stabilize stacked layers.

subtopics.title: Trace masked attention for two tokens

topics.title: Query, Key, and Value Intuition
topics.description: Queries and keys determine scores. Values supply the vectors that are mixed. In self-attention, all three can be projected from the same sequence with different learned weights.

topics.title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
topics.description: Scaling the query-key product by the square root of the key dimension keeps large dot products from growing as quickly with dimension. Apply the mask before softmax so disallowed positions receive no probability.

topics.title: Multi-Head Attention
topics.description: Different heads use different projections, so they can weight the same tokens differently. Concatenate head outputs along feature width and project back into the model representation size.

topics.title: Transformer Blocks
topics.description: A transformer block usually has attention and a feed-forward sublayer with residual connections. Attention can exchange information across permitted positions. The feed-forward path acts on each token representation separately.

topics.title: Normalization, Residual Connections, and Feed-Forward Layers
topics.description: A residual path adds a sublayer result to its input and therefore requires compatible dimensions. Layer normalization commonly normalizes features within each token representation. Feed-forward layers can temporarily widen the feature dimension.

subtopics.title: Normalization, Residual Connections, and Feed-Forward Layers

topics.title: Decoder-Only Transformer Architecture
topics.description: A decoder-only model processes a prefix with causal attention. The last position's logits describe possible next tokens. Generation chooses a token, appends it and repeats until a stopping condition or budget is met.

topics.title: Next-Token Prediction
topics.description: Next-token training pairs each position with the following token. During generation the chosen next token becomes part of the prefix, so later probabilities depend on earlier choices.

topics.title: Pretraining and Training Data Concepts
topics.description: Pretraining adjusts weights over a broad corpus using a learning objective. Data coverage affects what patterns the model can learn. A model may still produce plausible outputs about areas where its training evidence was weak.

topics.title: Instruction Tuning and Supervised Fine-Tuning
topics.description: Instruction tuning uses examples of requested behavior. For an assistant, formatting commonly identifies system, user and assistant messages. The training objective can focus on generating the expected assistant response.

topics.title: Preference Optimization Concepts
topics.description: Preference data compares candidate responses to the same prompt. Some methods train a reward model and optimize against it, while direct preference methods can use the comparisons without a separate reinforcement-learning loop.

topics.title: Fine-Tuning Fundamentals
topics.description: Fine-tuning updates a model for a dataset or behavior. It can overfit a small set or regress on unrelated cases. Compare it against a baseline on independent evidence before treating an observed change as useful.

topics.title: LoRA and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
topics.description: LoRA represents a weight update as the product of two smaller trainable matrices. It can freeze the base model and store the update separately. Loading that adapter still requires a compatible base architecture and weights.

topics.title: Hugging Face Tokenizers, Models, and Datasets
topics.description: A model, tokenizer and dataset can have different repositories and revisions. Verify compatibility and license before loading. Pin revisions so a later change does not silently change the fixture result.

subtopics.title: Hugging Face Tokenizers, Models, and Datasets

topics.title: Model Checkpoints and Model Weights
topics.description: Weights store learned tensors. Configuration defines how to interpret them and the tokenizer maps text into the expected IDs. Training resume may additionally need optimizer state and an iteration position.

topics.title: Context Windows and Context Limits
topics.description: The context window bounds the token sequence the model can handle in one request. System messages, history and retrieved evidence compete for space with the generated output. Make the packing policy explicit.

topics.title: Sampling, Temperature, and Top-P
topics.description: Temperature rescales logits before probabilities are computed. Top-p keeps a high-probability prefix sufficient to reach a threshold. Greedy decoding chooses the most likely token under the current scores.

topics.title: Quantization Fundamentals
topics.description: Lower-bit representations can reduce weight storage. Actual memory and speed depend on metadata, runtime support and operations performed at different precisions. Check behavior on the workload before choosing the smaller artifact.

topics.title: Model Size, RAM, VRAM, and Memory Requirements
topics.description: Parameter count times bytes per parameter gives an approximate dense weight budget. Runtime allocations, cache and concurrency can raise peak memory. The device needs enough headroom for the intended workload.

subtopics.title: Model Size, RAM, VRAM, and Memory Requirements

topics.title: LLM Inference Lifecycle
topics.description: An inference engine processes the prompt, then generates one or more successive tokens. It can reuse attention key and value state from earlier positions. Stopping and cancellation determine when request resources can be released.

topics.title: Latency, Throughput, and Tokens per Second
topics.description: Time to first token measures how long a client waits for output to start. End-to-end latency includes completion. Aggregate tokens per second divides total generated tokens by the workload interval, which differs from one stream's generation rate.

subtopics.title: Latency, Throughput, and Tokens per Second

topics.title: LLM Cost and Token Economics
topics.description: Input and output can have different unit rates. A retry can add usage even if the client received no completed response. Account for the attempt and distinguish provider-reported usage from a pre-call estimate.

topics.title: Hosted and Local Model Execution Concepts
topics.description: A hosted model is reached over a provider interface and can impose external quotas or retention policies. A local runtime lets the operator control more of the execution path while taking responsibility for capacity, updates and availability.

subtopics.title: Hosted and Local Model Execution Concepts

topics.title: Model Limitations, Hallucinations, and Knowledge Boundaries
topics.description: A model can produce fluent text from learned patterns even when relevant evidence is missing. Compare its claims against an authorized source and define a visible no-evidence response for unsupported requests.

subtopics.title: Model Limitations, Hallucinations, and Knowledge Boundaries

title: Python Backend Engineering for AI Systems
purpose: Build and test a documented, authenticated FastAPI service backed by PostgreSQL.
why: Build and test a documented, authenticated FastAPI service backed by PostgreSQL.
outcomes: Package the API for review and demonstrate startup, persistence and safe failure behavior in a fresh environment.
The handoff includes reproducible commands, migration order, evidence of a scoped request and the failure recovery steps.

topics.title: Backend Architecture and Service Responsibilities
topics.description: The transport adapter reads HTTP, the service enforces application rules and the storage adapter writes data. A separate service contract allows tests to exercise ownership decisions before bringing up the web or database layers.

topics.title: HTTP Methods, Status Codes, Headers, and Request Lifecycle
topics.description: HTTP sends a method and target with headers and optional content. The status and response body describe the result. Request authentication, body parsing and response serialization occur at different points along the service path.

subtopics.title: HTTP Methods, Status Codes, Headers, and Request Lifecycle

topics.title: REST API Design Principles and Resource Modeling
topics.description: A resource represents something a client can identify and interact with using HTTP methods. A task collection and a task instance have different targets. A webhook is a separate delivery to a consumer and needs its own verification and retry policy.

subtopics.title: REST API Design Principles and Resource Modeling

topics.title: FastAPI Project Setup and Application Structure
topics.description: The FastAPI application holds router registrations and service wiring. Keep startup configuration separate from route implementation. A test client can exercise the same routing and validation behavior without a network deployment.

subtopics.title: FastAPI Project Setup and Application Structure

topics.title: Path, Query, and Request Parameters
topics.description: A path parameter identifies a resource, query parameters can shape a read and a body carries structured input for a write. Typed constraints reject values before the handler depends on them.

topics.title: Request and Response Models with Pydantic
topics.description: Request and response models can express different contracts. An input may accept a secret for initial processing, while the public response should expose only selected fields. Define and test the public projection explicitly.

subtopics.title: Request and Response Models with Pydantic

topics.title: Validation, Serialization, and Safe Error Responses
topics.description: Validation protects later logic from unsupported shapes and sizes. A useful error identifies the failed field or constraint while avoiding credentials, full submitted payloads and internal tracebacks.

subtopics.title: Validation, Serialization, and Safe Error Responses

topics.title: OpenAPI and Interactive API Documentation
topics.description: OpenAPI describes operations, parameters, models and responses in a machine-readable document. Keep the generated contract close to the implementation and verify the parts clients depend on.

topics.title: Dependency Injection in FastAPI
topics.description: Dependency injection lets a route declare a required collaborator. Tests can substitute a provider without editing route logic. Resource ownership still belongs to the provider or enclosing lifecycle scope.

topics.title: Middleware and Request Lifecycle Hooks
topics.description: Middleware wraps request handling. It can attach context before calling the inner application and observe the response afterward. Cleanup or error accounting must cover failures as well as successful returns.

topics.title: Centralized Error Handling
topics.description: A service can raise a domain error without importing HTTP types. A central handler converts it to a documented status and public body. Unexpected failures should expose enough reference for diagnosis while protecting internals.

topics.title: Application Configuration and Environment Management
topics.description: Settings determine runtime behavior such as dependency endpoints and timeouts. Parse and validate them at startup so a missing value cannot be discovered only after receiving traffic.

topics.title: Secure Secret Handling
topics.description: A provider key belongs on the service side and should be loaded at runtime. Redact it from errors and observability payloads. Exercise a failure path because that is where request headers and raw exceptions are often exposed.

topics.title: Authentication Fundamentals
topics.description: Authentication establishes who made a request. API credentials can identify a service account, while a user credential represents a user. Route handlers should receive the authenticated principal from a verified dependency.

topics.title: Password Hashing and Credential Safety
topics.description: Password hashing functions deliberately make guesses expensive and use salts to distinguish equal passwords. Use a maintained implementation and store its encoded result. A login failure should avoid leaking the existence of a particular account.

topics.title: JWT Concepts and Secure Token Handling
topics.description: A JWT can carry claims signed by a trusted issuer. Decoding alone does not verify them. The service must check the signature and intended claims with an explicitly configured key and algorithm policy.

subtopics.title: JWT Concepts and Secure Token Handling

topics.title: OAuth 2.0 Concepts and External Identity Flows (focus on using and securing standard flows, not implementing the protocol from scratch)
topics.description: OAuth authorizes access to resources. OpenID Connect adds an identity layer. In an authorization-code flow, PKCE binds the code exchange to the client initiation, while a state value can bind the callback to the originating transaction.

subtopics.title: OAuth 2.0 Concepts and External Identity Flows (focus on using and securing standard flows, not implementing the protocol from scratch)

topics.title: Authorization and Role-Based Access Control
topics.description: Authorization determines what an authenticated principal can do. Roles describe capability, while ownership identifies which resources are in scope. Both checks are needed for a tenant-scoped operation.

topics.title: Secure Session and User-Access Design
topics.description: A session identifier refers to server-side login state. Secure cookie attributes limit transport and script exposure. When cookies are sent automatically, state-changing requests need a CSRF defense appropriate to the application.

topics.title: PostgreSQL Integration
topics.description: A database-backed API should establish a storage boundary with its own configuration and permissions. Make tenant identity part of every scoped query and use a local fixture to exercise actual constraints.

topics.title: SQLAlchemy ORM/Core and Safe Query Practices
topics.description: A Pydantic model checks request shape, SQLAlchemy executes relational work through a scoped session and Alembic versions schema changes. A successful response should follow a successful commit.

subtopics.title: Add a PostgreSQL-backed FastAPI endpoint with a reversible migration

topics.title: Alembic Database Migrations
topics.description: Alembic revisions describe ordered schema changes. Test the upgrade from the version a service already uses. Data conversion and rolling application changes may require staged compatibility, even when a schema downgrade is possible.

topics.title: Transactions, Connection Pools, and Database Session Lifecycle
topics.description: A database session scopes interactions with the transaction and connection pool. Keep ownership explicit, roll back on a failed unit of work and release the session even when request processing raises.

subtopics.title: Transactions, Connection Pools, and Database Session Lifecycle

topics.title: Async FastAPI Endpoints: when to use async def and when synchronous endpoints are appropriate
topics.description: An async handler can yield while it waits for an async dependency. Calling a blocking helper directly inside it can stall the event loop. A synchronous FastAPI handler can use a framework-managed thread for suitable blocking work.

subtopics.title: Async FastAPI Endpoints: when to use async def and when synchronous endpoints are appropriate

topics.title: Async Database and HTTP Client Usage
topics.description: An asynchronous HTTP client can be shared across requests when its lifecycle is owned by the app. A database session carries mutable transaction state and should be scoped to one task or request instead of shared across concurrent operations.

subtopics.title: Async Database and HTTP Client Usage

topics.title: Concurrency Limits for Slow LLM/API Calls: semaphores, request timeouts, and provider quotas
topics.description: A semaphore limits in-flight calls within a process. It does not enforce a provider's fleet-wide quota. Combine local admission with timeouts and explicit quota responses so waits and retries do not consume an unbounded deadline.

subtopics.title: Concurrency Limits for Slow LLM/API Calls: semaphores, request timeouts, and provider quotas

topics.title: Avoiding Blocking I/O Inside Async Endpoints
topics.description: A blocking function can occupy the event loop thread until it returns. Awaitable I/O yields execution while it waits. When a legacy dependency has no async interface, use a bounded offload or choose a synchronous handler.

subtopics.title: Avoiding Blocking I/O Inside Async Endpoints

topics.title: Thread Pools and Process Pools in Backend Workloads: when background execution is appropriate
topics.description: Threads can keep a request loop free while waiting for blocking I/O. A separate process can execute CPU work independently but adds startup and data-transfer costs. Bound outstanding submissions in either design.

subtopics.title: Thread Pools and Process Pools in Backend Workloads: when background execution is appropriate

topics.title: Background Tasks vs Durable Job Queues: understand the reliability boundary
topics.description: An in-process task can run after sending a response but shares the life of that process. A durable job is recorded before acknowledging acceptance and can be retried by a worker after interruption.

subtopics.title: Background Tasks vs Durable Job Queues: understand the reliability boundary

topics.title: Server-Sent Events and Streaming Responses for token-by-token output
topics.description: Server-sent events carry text event frames from server to client over HTTP. Token chunks can arrive before generation ends. Define an explicit completion or failure signal and release resources when the client disconnects.

subtopics.title: Server-Sent Events and Streaming Responses for token-by-token output

topics.title: WebSocket Fundamentals and Appropriate Use Cases (working knowledge, not a separate specialization)
topics.description: A WebSocket can keep a connection open for messages in both directions. A one-way response stream can often stay within HTTP streaming. Persistent connections require lifecycle, authorization and reconnect handling.

subtopics.title: WebSocket Fundamentals and Appropriate Use Cases (working knowledge, not a separate specialization)

topics.title: Pagination, Filtering, and API Versioning
topics.description: Pagination needs a stable sort order. Include a unique tie-breaker so equal sort values are deterministic. Validate client-controlled limits and filters before building the database query.

topics.title: Idempotent API Design and Safe Retry Behavior
topics.description: A client can retry when it does not know whether a write committed. Persist the idempotency key and result with the write, scope it to the operation and owner, and reject reuse with a conflicting request.

subtopics.title: Idempotent API Design and Safe Retry Behavior

topics.title: Unit and Integration Testing for APIs
topics.description: A service unit test isolates domain logic. A transport test exercises request and response contracts. A database integration test proves real constraints and transaction behavior that a fake cannot reproduce.

subtopics.title: Unit and Integration Testing for APIs

topics.title: API Logging, Request IDs, and Correlation IDs
topics.description: Structured logs store searchable fields such as route, duration and status. A correlation ID links related events across service boundaries. Validate external IDs and avoid fields containing credentials or private payloads.

subtopics.title: API Logging, Request IDs, and Correlation IDs

topics.title: Health Checks, Readiness Checks, and Graceful Shutdown
topics.description: Liveness asks whether the process can continue. Readiness asks whether it can accept work now. During shutdown, stop accepting new work and give in-flight requests a documented time to finish before cleanup.

subtopics.title: Health Checks, Readiness Checks, and Graceful Shutdown

topics.title: API Rate-Limit Integration and Handling Provider Rate Limits
topics.description: A service can reject requests before calling its provider. An upstream provider can also return a quota response. Distinguish these cases in telemetry and follow a bounded policy using any applicable retry hint.

subtopics.title: API Rate-Limit Integration and Handling Provider Rate Limits

topics.title: Building a Deployment-Ready FastAPI Service
topics.description: A deployment-ready service has a clear startup command, environment contract, migration procedure and readiness checks. Reproduce those steps from a clean environment so the setup does not depend on a developer's machine state.

title: LLM Application Engineering, Data Ingestion, RAG, Agents, MCP, and AI Safety
purpose: Ship a bounded AI workflow with provider adapters, authorized retrieval, tools, safety and regression evaluation.
why: Ship a bounded AI workflow with provider adapters, authorized retrieval, tools, safety and regression evaluation.
