outcomes: Design and test visible failure outcomes for an LLM workflow under timeout, overload and unsupported evidence.
Users can distinguish retryable issues from lack of evidence, internal details stay private and each failure is observable.

topics.title: Calling an LLM API from Python
topics.description: A provider client serializes the model request and receives response data and status. Keep the application contract small enough to verify against a fake provider before enabling live requests.

subtopics.title: Calling an LLM API from Python

topics.title: API Authentication and Secure Key Management
topics.description: Provider credentials authorize the service, so use server-side runtime injection. Avoid including headers in exception bodies. A rotation test confirms the service can adopt a new value without storing the old one.

subtopics.title: API Authentication and Secure Key Management

topics.title: Provider-Neutral Adapter Design
topics.description: An adapter translates your domain request to a provider's format. Store which options each provider supports. Normalize response and failure data so callers can depend on a stable application contract.

topics.title: Prompt Engineering Fundamentals
topics.description: State the requested task, relevant context and expected output. An example can clarify ambiguous formatting, but should be tested against examples that differ from it.

topics.title: System Instructions and User Messages
topics.description: A provider may distinguish application instructions from user messages. Structure makes the intended roles visible. Tool authorization and data access still depend on enforced application controls.

topics.title: Structured Outputs and Schema Validation
topics.description: A provider may help constrain output shape. The application must still validate the payload and check business meaning. A syntactically correct object can carry a forbidden value.

topics.title: Function Calling and Tool Calling
topics.description: A model can propose a tool name and arguments. The host chooses whether to execute the proposal. Dispatch through a known tool registry and validate data and authority before invoking the code.

topics.title: Streaming LLM Responses
topics.description: Streaming can expose partial output before the request succeeds. Track completion explicitly and release upstream resources when a client leaves or an error terminates the stream.

topics.title: Token Budgeting and Context Management
topics.description: An input budget includes instructions, user text, retained history and tool or retrieval context. Reserve response tokens separately. Keep the model and tokenizer assumptions visible.

topics.title: Model Selection and Model Routing
topics.description: Filter models by required capability and context before scoring eligible choices. A deterministic tie-breaker keeps behavior predictable. Make the reason visible for evaluation.

subtopics.title: Easy, medium, and complex task levels

topics.title: Provider Fallback and Failure Handling
topics.description: Fallback can improve availability when a provider is temporarily unavailable. It can also multiply cost or change capability. Check deadline, compatibility and policy before issuing a second attempt.

topics.title: Retries, Timeouts, Exponential Backoff, and Jitter
topics.description: Backoff spaces out retry attempts and jitter reduces synchronized retries. A per-call timeout limits one attempt, while the overall deadline limits the operation including waits.

subtopics.title: Retries, Timeouts, Exponential Backoff, and Jitter

topics.title: Token Usage Tracking
topics.description: Usage can arrive with the final response or be absent after failure. Record whether counts are reported or estimated. Keep request and attempt identities separate so retries remain attributable.

topics.title: Cost Accounting and Per-User Usage Limits
topics.description: A request budget can reserve expected usage before calling a provider. Reconcile with actual reported usage after completion. Scope reserves to the correct user and handle delayed or unavailable usage explicitly.

subtopics.title: Cost Accounting and Per-User Usage Limits

topics.title: LLM Application Logging and Tracing
topics.description: Capture request identity once and propagate it through adapter attempts. Useful telemetry includes model, duration and failure class. Avoid putting raw prompts or secrets in diagnostic fields.

topics.title: Structured vs Unstructured Data and Common AI Data Sources
topics.description: A CSV has row and column structure, while a text PDF typically carries visual layout instructions. You can retain both as normalized text for search, but the original row or page locator is still needed to cite an answer.

subtopics.title: Structured vs Unstructured Data and Common AI Data Sources

topics.title: ETL/ELT Fundamentals and the Data Pipeline Lifecycle
topics.description: In ETL, transform the input before loading into the destination. ELT loads a raw copy first and transforms near storage. Keeping a raw copy can support replay, provided the data policy permits the copy and deletion propagates to it.

subtopics.title: ETL/ELT Fundamentals and the Data Pipeline Lifecycle

topics.title: Ingestion Pipeline Design: source → extract → normalize → clean → validate → enrich → chunk → embed → index
topics.description: Carry source identity from extraction through indexing. A parser returns text blocks, a normalizer makes them comparable, and a validator rejects empty or malformed records. The index stores searchable representations linked back to authorized source locations.

subtopics.title: Ingestion Pipeline Design: source → extract → normalize → clean → validate → enrich → chunk → embed → index

topics.title: Extracting Text from PDFs with pypdf (including limitations of scanned/image-only PDFs)
topics.description: Use PdfReader to inspect pages and page.extract_text() to recover encoded text. A scanned page may contain pixels with no useful text layer. Track page index, returned text and extraction status separately so an empty extraction cannot silently disappear.

subtopics.title: Extracting Text from PDFs with pypdf (including limitations of scanned/image-only PDFs)

topics.title: Extracting and Cleaning HTML with BeautifulSoup
topics.description: Select the main content element before getting text. Extract each heading and following paragraphs as a section so that a quotation has a useful locator. Handle a missing main element explicitly instead of letting boilerplate become the searchable record.

subtopics.title: Extracting and Cleaning HTML with BeautifulSoup

topics.title: Handling Markdown, TXT, CSV, JSON, and DOCX Documents
topics.description: Text, Markdown, CSV and JSON differ in structure even when stored as plain text bytes. Parse structured formats before flattening. DOCX text may be in paragraphs and tables, so a plain text reader cannot recover its intended record boundaries.

subtopics.title: Handling Markdown, TXT, CSV, JSON, and DOCX Documents

topics.title: Reading Documents from APIs and exported knowledge bases; understand a Notion-like source as an API/export integration, not as a separate technology track
topics.description: A knowledge-base API can provide page IDs and update timestamps, while an export can provide those fields in a manifest. A connector should report a partial traversal and keep a durable checkpoint for the last fully accepted page.

subtopics.title: Reading Documents from APIs and exported knowledge bases; understand a Notion-like source as an API/export integration, not as a separate technology track

topics.title: Audio Ingestion Concepts: transcription output, timestamps, speaker/segment metadata, and when audio belongs in a product. Do not make speech-model training a core requirement
topics.description: A transcript turns speech into text. A time span links retrieved text to its original audio segment, and a supplied speaker label may help contextualize it. Noisy audio or overlapping voices can reduce transcript and speaker accuracy.

subtopics.title: Audio Ingestion Concepts: transcription output, timestamps, speaker/segment metadata, and when audio belongs in a product. Do not make speech-model training a core requirement

topics.title: Text Normalization, Encoding, Whitespace, Tables, Headers, and Document Structure
topics.description: Normalize Unicode consistently before hashing or comparing text. Repeated blank lines can be collapsed within prose, while a table row boundary carries meaning. Keep structure and the locator beside the normalized content.

subtopics.title: Text Normalization, Encoding, Whitespace, Tables, Headers, and Document Structure

topics.title: Data Validation, Duplicate Detection, Metadata Extraction, and Source Tracking
topics.description: Use a source key for identity and a normalized content hash to detect a repeated payload. Scope both decisions to a tenant. Structural chunking can follow headings while semantic grouping can use a topic shift. Both need provenance even when their boundaries differ.

subtopics.title: Data Validation, Duplicate Detection, Metadata Extraction, and Source Tracking

topics.title: Batch vs Incremental Ingestion and Change Detection
topics.description: A full batch reads the whole source. Incremental runs use a cursor or high-water mark and handle tombstones explicitly. Timestamp equality can miss changes unless the cursor contains a stable tie-breaker or uses a safe overlap with deduplication.

subtopics.title: Batch vs Incremental Ingestion and Change Detection

topics.title: Idempotent Ingestion, Retries, Checkpoints, and Failed-Document Handling
topics.description: Build a staging revision and activate it transactionally after the checks pass. Reuse a stable tenant and source revision key on retry. A permanent parse failure belongs in quarantine with a redacted reason so it cannot loop indefinitely.

subtopics.title: Idempotent Ingestion, Retries, Checkpoints, and Failed-Document Handling

topics.title: Secure Ingestion: access permissions, tenant boundaries, sensitive data, and deletion/update propagation
topics.description: Attach tenant identity from the authenticated context before staging bytes. An upstream delete must propagate to derived chunks, embeddings and caches under the retention policy. Authorization also applies at retrieval time because source permissions can change.

subtopics.title: Secure Ingestion: access permissions, tenant boundaries, sensitive data, and deletion/update propagation

topics.title: Data Quality Checks and Ingestion Observability
topics.description: Count records at the boundaries where a stage can reject them. A freshness measure such as age of the latest committed source revision complements error rate because a quiet pipeline can still be stale. Label metrics by bounded stage and outcome.

subtopics.title: Data Quality Checks and Ingestion Observability

topics.title: Embeddings Fundamentals
topics.description: An embedding represents text as a numeric vector generated by a model. Keep model and preprocessing identity with indexed vectors. Vectors from different embedding spaces should not be compared casually.

topics.title: Vector Similarity and Distance Measures
topics.description: Cosine compares direction while dot product also depends on magnitude. Euclidean distance orders smaller distances first. Confirm whether a database operator returns distance or similarity before interpreting the rank.

topics.title: Semantic Search
topics.description: Encode a query and candidate documents in compatible vector spaces. Search ranks vectors by closeness, which may find related wording. Relevance still depends on the task and needs independent judgment.

topics.title: Text Chunking Strategies: fixed-size, structure-aware, recursive, and semantic chunking
topics.description: Fixed chunks follow a size limit. Structural chunks follow document landmarks. Recursive splitting tries stronger separators first. Semantic splitting can use shifts in relatedness. Every chunk still needs a source locator.

subtopics.title: Text Chunking Strategies: fixed-size, structure-aware, recursive, and semantic chunking

topics.title: Chunk Size, Overlap, Metadata, and Retrieval Trade-Offs
topics.description: Overlap can preserve evidence spanning a boundary, but it can duplicate context and indexing work. Record source offsets so overlapping hits can be combined and cited correctly.

subtopics.title: Chunk Size, Overlap, Metadata, and Retrieval Trade-Offs

topics.title: Vector Indexing Concepts
topics.description: An exact search checks candidates directly. An approximate index can reduce search work at the cost of missing some neighbors. Measure against exact results with the same query set and filters.

topics.title: PostgreSQL with pgvector
topics.description: pgvector adds a vector type and distance operators to PostgreSQL. Establish an exact query before tuning an index. Apply authorization scope in the query so a correct distance cannot expose an unauthorized row.

topics.title: Retrieval Pipelines and Query Transformation Basics
topics.description: A retrieval pipeline can normalize or rewrite a query before encoding it. Rewriting may add useful context or accidentally change intent. Keep the original query available to evaluate the effect.

subtopics.title: Retrieval Pipelines and Query Transformation Basics

topics.title: Metadata Filtering and Access-Control-Aware Retrieval
topics.description: Relevance and authorization are separate. Apply permissions using trusted identity and source metadata before constructing model context. Test a tempting unauthorized match to prove the filter is effective.

topics.title: Hybrid Search Concepts
topics.description: Lexical search can find exact phrases or identifiers. Vector search can find related wording. A fusion rule combines ranks, which avoids directly comparing scores on unrelated scales.

topics.title: Reranking Fundamentals
topics.description: A reranker reorders candidates already retrieved. It can improve precision near the top, but cannot recover a document missing from the candidate pool. Include its latency in the comparison.

topics.title: RAG Architecture and End-to-End Data Flow
topics.description: RAG retrieves relevant source text at request time and supplies it as model context. Ingestion prepares searchable data independently. A correct workflow needs an explicit result when suitable authorized evidence is missing.

subtopics.title: RAG Architecture and End-to-End Data Flow

topics.title: RAG Context Construction, Source Attribution, and Citation Handling
topics.description: Attach stable source references as you pack evidence. A model can emit a plausible citation ID that was never provided. Check that a citation resolves to a permitted chunk and supports the associated claim.

subtopics.title: RAG Context Construction, Source Attribution, and Citation Handling

topics.title: RAG Evaluation Datasets and Expected Answers
topics.description: A RAG evaluation fixture records what evidence should support each answer. Include cases where no authorized answer exists. Version both dataset and corpus so metrics remain interpretable.

subtopics.title: RAG Evaluation Datasets and Expected Answers

topics.title: Retrieval Quality Metrics and Failure Analysis
topics.description: Retrieval recall asks how much expected evidence was found. Precision asks how much retrieved evidence was expected. Inspect failures by stage to distinguish missing indexed content from a ranking or filtering issue.

subtopics.title: Retrieval Quality Metrics and Failure Analysis

topics.title: Hallucination Reduction and Grounded Responses
topics.description: A relevant answer can still include unsupported details. Compare claims to the actual evidence and define when to abstain. Evaluate both answer quality and the system's behavior when sources are missing.

topics.title: Agent Fundamentals and Appropriate Use Cases
topics.description: An agent can select a next action from its observations and a goal. This introduces uncertainty and more failure paths. Use it when later actions genuinely depend on earlier observations.

subtopics.title: Agent Fundamentals and Appropriate Use Cases

topics.title: Deterministic Workflows vs Agentic Workflows
topics.description: A deterministic workflow encodes transitions in application code. An agentic workflow delegates some action selection to a model. A service can combine both by fixing safety-critical transitions and bounding model choices.

topics.title: Tool-Using Agents and Tool Contracts
topics.description: Describe what a tool reads or changes along with its schema. The host should validate a proposed call and the tool implementation should enforce its own resource boundary.

topics.title: Planning and Execution Loops
topics.description: A plan proposes a sequence of actions. An execution loop observes the result and can revise the next step. Limit steps, time and tool calls so repeated observations cannot cause unbounded work.

topics.title: Agent State and Context Management
topics.description: An agent state record tracks what the workflow knows and what work is complete. Keep it scoped to the authenticated session. Persist only information needed to resume safely.

topics.title: Memory Concepts, Scope, Expiration, and Memory Boundaries
topics.description: Working context is information available during a run. Durable memory may cross runs and must follow ownership and retention rules. Avoid granting retrieved memories authority over actions.

subtopics.title: Memory Concepts, Scope, Expiration, and Memory Boundaries

topics.title: Single-Agent Tool Workflow: build and evaluate one reliable agent
topics.description: A single agent can request a tool, observe the result and decide when to stop. Use a deterministic test provider to verify the workflow boundary before testing variable model output.

subtopics.title: Single-Agent Tool Workflow: build and evaluate one reliable agent

topics.title: Multi-Agent Systems: concepts, coordination overhead, and when multiple agents are justified
topics.description: Separate agents can specialize but need to exchange state and resolve conflicting results. Each handoff adds time, tokens and an additional failure boundary.

subtopics.title: Multi-Agent Systems: concepts, coordination overhead, and when multiple agents are justified

topics.title: Human Approval and Human-in-the-Loop Controls
topics.description: Human approval should show the intended target and effect. Bind approval to a specific action and its arguments. A new proposal needs its own decision when those details change.

topics.title: Agent Error Handling, Recovery, Tracing, and Evaluation
topics.description: Classify failure before choosing recovery. A transient error can justify retry under a budget. Denial is a policy result. Correlate attempts with state transitions so replay can be audited.

subtopics.title: Agent Error Handling, Recovery, Tracing, and Evaluation

topics.title: Model Context Protocol Fundamentals and the problem it solves
topics.description: MCP gives clients and servers a shared way to expose and use capabilities. The host still controls user experience and permissions. A shared protocol reduces repeated integration work when multiple hosts use the same capability.

subtopics.title: Model Context Protocol Fundamentals and the problem it solves

topics.title: MCP Hosts, Clients, and Servers
topics.description: The host manages the overall application and its policy. A client communicates with a server. The server exposes capabilities and enforces its own access to protected resources.

topics.title: MCP Tools, Resources, and Prompts
topics.description: Resources expose contextual data, prompts expose reusable templates and tools expose callable functions. Discovery helps inspect available capabilities and their contracts. Authority to use one is checked separately.

topics.title: MCP Transport and Lifecycle Concepts (working understanding; do not over-focus on protocol internals)
topics.description: A local stdio client can start and communicate with a server process. A remote HTTP transport adds network, identity and session boundaries. Initialize and check negotiated capabilities before depending on them.

subtopics.title: MCP Transport and Lifecycle Concepts (working understanding; do not over-focus on protocol internals)

topics.title: Building one MCP Server with the official Python SDK
topics.description: An MCP host owns the user session and policy. A client manages a protocol connection to a server. Tool discovery exposes schemas. Permission to discover a tool does not itself authorize an action.

subtopics.title: Exercise an official Python SDK MCP tool with an explicit permission boundary

topics.title: Connecting one MCP Client and invoking a tool safely
topics.description: A client initializes a session and can inspect the server's tool schemas. Choose from an application allowlist before invoking anything. Use a bounded deadline and close the session after success or failure.

subtopics.title: Connecting one MCP Client and invoking a tool safely

topics.title: Integrating an MCP server with the single-agent workflow
topics.description: An MCP adapter can implement the same application tool interface as a direct function. Keep validation and approval outside model text. Pass only authorized context across the server boundary.

subtopics.title: Integrating an MCP server with the single-agent workflow

topics.title: MCP Authentication, Authorization, Consent, and Tool Permissions
topics.description: User consent can permit a particular host action. Server authorization verifies the caller and resource scope independently. Discovery, a model proposal or a valid schema does not establish either authority.

subtopics.title: MCP Authentication, Authorization, Consent, and Tool Permissions

topics.title: Testing, Debugging, and Versioning an MCP Integration
topics.description: Treat the discovered schema and expected result as a contract. Pin known fixture versions and test changes explicitly. Capture failure boundaries without dumping arguments that may contain private data.

subtopics.title: Testing, Debugging, and Versioning an MCP Integration

topics.title: Building a Golden Evaluation Dataset
topics.description: A golden dataset is a versioned set of inputs and reviewed outcomes. Include common and consequential failures. Stable case IDs let reviewers compare results across revisions.

topics.title: Evaluating Structured Output and Tool-Calling Accuracy
topics.description: A schema test answers whether the data has the expected shape. Tool evaluation also checks the chosen action and argument meaning. Authorization needs its own outcome because a valid proposal can still be denied.

subtopics.title: Evaluating Structured Output and Tool-Calling Accuracy

topics.title: RAG Evaluation and Retrieval Regression Testing
topics.description: A RAG regression suite can check retrieval separately from answer behavior. Pin the corpus and expected evidence. A tenant-isolation failure should fail the suite regardless of aggregate answer quality.

subtopics.title: RAG Evaluation and Retrieval Regression Testing

topics.title: Agent Trajectory and Multi-Step Evaluation
topics.description: A trajectory records steps and tool outcomes. An answer may look correct despite an unsafe or wasteful process. Inspect policy decisions and budgets separately from the final result.

topics.title: Regression Evaluation Before Model or Prompt Changes
topics.description: Evaluate proposed changes against the same inputs and rubric used for the baseline. Record both revisions, run assumptions and the rule for accepting the trade-off.

subtopics.title: Regression Evaluation Before Model or Prompt Changes

topics.title: Prompt Injection and Indirect Prompt Injection
topics.description: Direct injection arrives in user input. Indirect injection can arrive through documents or tool responses. Treat those inputs as data and enforce action and resource policies outside the model.

subtopics.title: Prompt Injection and Indirect Prompt Injection

topics.title: Unsafe Tool Execution and Permission Boundaries
topics.description: A tool executor accepts only known operations under explicit permissions. Avoid treating model-produced text as executable code. The tool server should independently enforce resource scope.

subtopics.title: Unsafe Tool Execution and Permission Boundaries

topics.title: Data Leakage and Sensitive Information Protection
topics.description: LLM systems can disclose data through retrieval, generated responses and diagnostics. Enforce data access before context is built and verify output and telemetry under a controlled failure.

subtopics.title: Data Leakage and Sensitive Information Protection

topics.title: Input Validation, Output Validation, and Guardrails
topics.description: Check input shape and limits before spending resources. Validate model outputs before rendering, querying or executing actions. Treat semantic checks and permissions separately from structure.

subtopics.title: Input Validation, Output Validation, and Guardrails

topics.title: Human Review for High-Impact Actions
topics.description: A review step gives a human the relevant context and a chance to decline. Record the proposed action, reviewer scope and decision. Expired or altered proposals require a new review.

topics.title: LLM Reliability, Failure Modes, and User-Facing Error Design
topics.description: A user-facing error should state what happened at a useful level and whether retry is appropriate. Timeout, quota and missing evidence have different recovery paths. Correlate safe user messages with internal diagnostics.

subtopics.title: LLM Reliability, Failure Modes, and User-Facing Error Design

title: System Design and Distributed Systems
purpose: Use measured workloads and failure scenarios to design caches, limits, queues and service boundaries.
why: Use measured workloads and failure scenarios to design caches, limits, queues and service boundaries.
outcomes: Design an AI workload targeting one million daily requests and separate capacity estimates from demonstrated measurements.
The report includes capacity equations, provider limits, backpressure, database operations, measured workloads, failure behavior and a clear separation between the design target and tested capacity.

topics.title: Introduction to System Design and How to Approach a Design Question
topics.description: Start with a concrete use case, then define request, data and reliability expectations. Sketch only the components needed for that workload. Record a decision and the evidence that could change it.

subtopics.title: Introduction to System Design and How to Approach a Design Question

topics.title: Functional and Non-Functional Requirements
topics.description: A functional requirement says what the service should do. A quality requirement says how it should behave under a stated workload or failure. Both need observable acceptance criteria.

topics.title: Requirement Clarification and Scope Definition
topics.description: Design depends on choices such as who can read documents and how quickly a deletion takes effect. Make the assumptions visible so two readers can evaluate the same proposed behavior.

topics.title: Capacity Estimation and Back-of-the-Envelope Calculations
topics.description: Divide volume by its time window for average rate. Peaks depend on how activity is distributed. Multiply requests by per-request bytes or work to estimate capacity under both average and peak assumptions.

topics.title: Requests per Second, Throughput, Concurrency, and Workload Shape
topics.description: Arrival rate measures incoming work, while throughput measures completed work. In a stable system, average in-flight work relates to rate times average time in the system. A burst can temporarily invalidate a steady-state estimate.

subtopics.title: Requests per Second, Throughput, Concurrency, and Workload Shape

topics.title: Average, p95, and p99 Latency
topics.description: A percentile describes a boundary in the latency distribution. An average can conceal a few long waits. Report the sample count, quantile method and treatment of failures alongside the result.

topics.title: Availability, Reliability, and Durability
topics.description: An endpoint can be reachable and still return incorrect results. A temporarily unavailable service can retain durable data. Separate these outcomes because each calls for a different reliability control.

topics.title: Service-Level Indicators and Objectives (basic purpose and examples)
topics.description: An SLI measures a behavior such as the share of eligible requests completed within a deadline. An SLO gives that indicator a target for a window. The remaining allowance is its error budget.

subtopics.title: Service-Level Indicators and Objectives (basic purpose and examples)

topics.title: Modular Monoliths, Separation of Responsibilities, and Clear Service Boundaries
topics.description: A modular monolith deploys as one application while maintaining internal ownership boundaries. Keeping modules behind explicit interfaces helps test their behavior and makes a later service split an evidence-based option.

subtopics.title: Modular Monoliths, Separation of Responsibilities, and Clear Service Boundaries

topics.title: Stateless and Stateful Services
topics.description: A stateless request handler can process any valid request using its inputs and shared dependencies. State can still exist in the system. Moving it outside the replica changes where availability and consistency must be checked.

topics.title: Horizontal and Vertical Scaling
topics.description: Vertical scaling increases resources available to a single instance. Horizontal scaling adds replicas. Neither necessarily improves throughput when the bottleneck sits in a shared database or provider.

topics.title: Reverse Proxies and Load Balancing Concepts
topics.description: A reverse proxy accepts client requests and forwards them to upstreams. A load balancer chooses an available target under a policy. The service must know which proxy is trusted to supply forwarded metadata.

subtopics.title: Reverse Proxies and Load Balancing Concepts

topics.title: Database Indexing and Connection Pool Impacts on Capacity
topics.description: A larger pool can remove app-side waiting until the database saturates. A selective index can reduce work per query at the cost of storage and write maintenance. Measure both bottlenecks under the same workload.

subtopics.title: Database Indexing and Connection Pool Impacts on Capacity

topics.title: Caching Fundamentals, Cache Keys, TTL, and Cache-Aside
topics.description: On a cache-aside miss, the application reads the source and may store the result under a key with expiry. The source stays authoritative. Include version and authorization scope when those affect the result.

subtopics.title: Caching Fundamentals, Cache Keys, TTL, and Cache-Aside

topics.title: Redis Fundamentals and Core Data Structures
topics.description: Redis data structures expose different operations. A string can store one serialized cache item. A sorted set supports score-based ranking. Choose by required access pattern and clean up owned fixture keys.

subtopics.title: Redis Fundamentals and Core Data Structures

topics.title: Implementing one Redis-backed cache in a FastAPI service
topics.description: Treat a cache as an optimization for suitable reads. If it cannot be reached, an application can fall back to the source within a deadline when policy permits. Confirm that failure does not bypass authorization.

subtopics.title: Implementing one Redis-backed cache in a FastAPI service

topics.title: Cache Invalidation, Expiration, and Common Cache Failure Modes
topics.description: Expiration bounds a cache item's lifetime. Invalidation responds to a change. If many callers miss together, the source may receive a burst. A strategy should account for both staleness and load.

subtopics.title: Cache Invalidation, Expiration, and Common Cache Failure Modes

topics.title: Rate-Limiting Fundamentals and Per-User/API Quotas
topics.description: A limit describes who is counted, what requests consume capacity and how much burst is acceptable. An IP address can represent many users, so identity and fairness depend on the application contract.

topics.title: Implementing a basic token-bucket or fixed/sliding-window rate limiter
topics.description: A token bucket refills over time up to its capacity. Each admitted request consumes tokens. With an injected clock, edge cases such as partial refill and long inactivity are deterministic.

subtopics.title: Implementing a basic token-bucket or fixed/sliding-window rate limiter

topics.title: Redis Atomic Operations and Why Race Conditions Matter
topics.description: Reading a value, incrementing it in application code and writing it back creates an interleaving window. Redis INCR updates the counter atomically. Updating a counter and its expiry together may require a larger atomic boundary.

subtopics.title: Redis Atomic Operations and Why Race Conditions Matter

topics.title: Distributed Rate Limiting with Redis
topics.description: Per-process counters multiply a nominal limit across replicas. A shared Redis decision gives callers one state boundary. Its loss creates an application decision about availability and protection that must be measured.

topics.title: Redis Lua Scripting for an atomic distributed rate limiter (advanced hands-on exercise)
topics.description: A token bucket adds capacity over time up to a limit. Two requests can both spend the last token if they read and update separately. A Redis Lua script can make a small read-decide-write operation atomic on the server.

subtopics.title: Make a Redis token-bucket decision atomic

topics.title: Background Jobs, Worker Concepts, and Durable Queue Requirements
topics.description: A durable job is recorded before an API acknowledges acceptance. A worker takes responsibility for execution and acknowledges only after the defined commit boundary. Restart behavior follows that boundary.

subtopics.title: Background Jobs, Worker Concepts, and Durable Queue Requirements

topics.title: Retries, Exponential Backoff, Dead-Letter Handling, and Poison Messages
topics.description: Retries can absorb transient faults but consume capacity. Delay attempts with backoff and apply a cap. A permanently invalid payload belongs in a terminal or dead-letter path with a useful redacted reason.

subtopics.title: Retries, Exponential Backoff, Dead-Letter Handling, and Poison Messages

topics.title: Idempotency and Duplicate Request/Event Handling
topics.description: Retries can repeat an event whose first execution already committed. Store a stable identity and the side effect in a coordinated transaction so a retry can identify the previous outcome.

topics.title: Timeouts, Circuit Breakers, Bulkheads, and Graceful Degradation
topics.description: A deadline limits waiting, while a circuit breaker can temporarily avoid repeated failing calls. A bulkhead reserves independent resources so a failure in one dependency does not exhaust every path.

subtopics.title: Timeouts, Circuit Breakers, Bulkheads, and Graceful Degradation

topics.title: Backpressure and Bounded Work Queues
topics.description: When arrivals exceed service rate, queued work grows. Bound the queue and choose whether to delay, shed or reject work. Report overload before requests spend their whole deadline waiting.

topics.title: Database Replication
topics.description: Replication copies data to another node. With asynchronous replication, a replica can lag the primary and a promoted replica may lack recent writes. A read route should reflect the freshness a caller needs.

topics.title: Partitioning and Sharding: purpose, trade-offs, and operational cost
topics.description: Sharding distributes parts of a dataset across nodes. The key determines which operations are local. A popular tenant or time range can still concentrate load on one shard.

subtopics.title: Partitioning and Sharding: purpose, trade-offs, and operational cost

topics.title: Consistency Models
topics.description: A consistency model specifies what values reads can observe after writes. Replicas may converge later under eventual consistency. A session can require its own writes to be visible even when other readers tolerate lag.

topics.title: CAP Theorem and Practical Trade-Offs
topics.description: A network partition stops some replicas communicating. A service may reject operations to preserve a consistency guarantee, or continue some operations while accepting divergence that must be reconciled.

topics.title: Distributed Transactions and Sagas at an introductory architectural level
topics.description: A saga coordinates local transactions across services. A failed later step can trigger compensating business operations. A compensation has its own possible failures and should be tracked.

subtopics.title: Distributed Transactions and Sagas at an introductory architectural level

topics.title: Message Queues and Event-Driven Architecture
topics.description: A broker decouples when a producer publishes from when a consumer processes. An event describes something that happened, while a command requests a specific action. Consumers still need a delivery and failure policy.

topics.title: Kafka Fundamentals and When Kafka Is Justified
topics.description: Kafka stores events in partitioned logs for a configured retention period. Multiple consumer groups can read the same retained events at their own progress. That capability carries additional infrastructure and operational cost.

subtopics.title: Kafka Fundamentals and When Kafka Is Justified

topics.title: Kafka Topics, Partitions, and Consumer Groups
topics.description: A topic contains partitions, and ordering is defined within each partition. Members of one consumer group divide partition ownership. Separate groups keep independent progress through the stream.

subtopics.title: Kafka Topics, Partitions, and Consumer Groups

topics.title: Asynchronous Workers and Consumer Processing
topics.description: A consumer reads events and may persist a result. The offset is a progress marker. Advancing it ahead of durable processing can lose work, while committing afterward can produce a replay that needs idempotency.

topics.title: Ordering, Consumer Lag, Replay, and Delivery Semantics
topics.description: A consumer may see an event again after it finishes work but fails before saving its offset. Store a stable event ID with the durable result so a repeated delivery can be recognized.

topics.title: Service-to-Service Communication
topics.description: A synchronous call keeps a dependency on the request path. A queued message can decouple timing but introduces delivery and eventual visibility concerns. Discovery provides addresses, while the interface still defines accepted behavior.

topics.title: Microservices Fundamentals and the operational cost of splitting services
topics.description: A network service can have independent releases and capacity. The split also introduces network failure, compatibility and observability responsibilities that were previously inside one process.

subtopics.title: Microservices Fundamentals and the operational cost of splitting services

topics.title: Distributed Tracing and Request Correlation
topics.description: A trace connects related spans across services. A span records one operation and its timing. Propagating context lets a reader follow the request even when logs originate from separate processes.

topics.title: Multi-Tenant Architecture and Tenant Isolation
topics.description: A shared database, cache and queue can serve several tenants. Every derived key and authorization decision must retain tenant context. Resource limits may also be needed to keep one tenant's workload from consuming shared capacity.

topics.title: Cost, Capacity, and Performance Trade-Offs
topics.description: A design can be cheaper per token and more expensive per completed request if it retries often or requires more tokens. Compare quality, throughput and failure behavior against the same user workload.

topics.title: Designing and measuring AI API workloads at increasing traffic levels
topics.description: An AI API can saturate at admission, database work, provider quotas or generation. Increase workload in controlled steps and observe both request and token metrics. A higher incoming rate can create queue growth without raising successful throughput.

subtopics.title: Designing and measuring AI API workloads at increasing traffic levels

topics.title: Designing an AI platform targeting one million requests per day, with explicit average/peak calculations, model-provider limits, token cost, queueing, database load, and load-test evidence
topics.description: One million requests per day averages about 11.57 requests per second, but the busiest period may be much higher. Estimate input and output token demand, retries and provider limits before choosing concurrency and queue capacity. Record what the load test actually sustained.

subtopics.title: Designing an AI platform targeting one million requests per day, with explicit average/peak calculations, model-provider limits, token cost, queueing, database load, and load-test evidence

title: Production Engineering, Cloud, MLOps, LLMOps, Security, and Observability
purpose: Deploy, measure and recover an AI service with containers, AWS, infrastructure as code and operational controls.
why: Deploy, measure and recover an AI service with containers, AWS, infrastructure as code and operational controls.
outcomes: Review a fixture release against production readiness criteria and verify a rollback end to end.
The review records a release decision with evidence, a demonstrated recovery path and open risks assigned to an owner.

topics.title: Linux for Production Services and SSH-Based Server Access
topics.description: SSH authenticates the server as well as the client. After confirming the host key, inspect the service status and its journal, then verify the listening socket. A running process bound to localhost can still be unreachable from outside.

subtopics.title: Linux for Production Services and SSH-Based Server Access

topics.title: Environment Configuration and Development/Staging/Production Separation
topics.description: Package code once and supply environment configuration separately. Validate required settings at startup. A service that defaults to a production endpoint after a typo can turn a local test into a real write.

topics.title: Secrets Management and Configuration Safety
topics.description: Separate references from values. Inject values when the service starts and avoid recording them in Dockerfile instructions, repository configuration or debugging output. Rotate and revoke a fixture credential to test how a consumer reloads it.

topics.title: Docker Fundamentals and Why Containers Are Used
topics.description: An image packages files and startup metadata. A container is a running or stopped instance with its own process and writable layer. Two instances can share one image while receiving different environment values.

subtopics.title: Docker Fundamentals and Why Containers Are Used

topics.title: Dockerfiles, Images, Containers, Ports, and Volumes
topics.description: A Dockerfile builds an image from its context. Publishing a port maps a host address to a container listener. A volume persists files outside the container's writable layer, so replacing the container need not remove its mounted data.

subtopics.title: Dockerfiles, Images, Containers, Ports, and Volumes

topics.title: Docker Compose for a Local FastAPI + PostgreSQL + Redis Stack
topics.description: Compose creates a network where services can discover each other by name. A started process is different from a ready dependency. Use health checks and a readiness-aware API so startup and restarts expose useful failure behavior.

subtopics.title: Docker Compose for a Local FastAPI + PostgreSQL + Redis Stack

topics.title: Container Logs, Health Checks, and Basic Resource Limits
topics.description: Containers normally expose process output through their logging driver. A health check can fail while the main process is still running. CPU or memory constraints are separate controls whose symptoms should be checked with runtime status and logs.

subtopics.title: Container Logs, Health Checks, and Basic Resource Limits

topics.title: CI/CD Fundamentals and Automated Test/Build Pipelines
topics.description: CI runs the same defined checks for proposed changes. A build artifact is meaningful only when its inputs and successful checks are traceable. Keep deployment credentials out of the basic test workflow.

subtopics.title: CI/CD Fundamentals and Automated Test/Build Pipelines

topics.title: Deploying a Small Python API to a basic AWS compute environment
topics.description: A small AWS compute instance can run an API process behind a limited ingress rule. The application reads configuration under its own runtime identity. Verify who can reach the listener, what the role can access and how to remove the resources after the exercise.

subtopics.title: Deploying a Small Python API to a basic AWS compute environment

topics.title: AWS Identity and Access Management Fundamentals
topics.description: An IAM role has a trust relationship and permissions. The trust relationship controls who can assume the role. The permissions determine which AWS operations the assumed role can perform on which resources.

subtopics.title: AWS Identity and Access Management Fundamentals

topics.title: AWS Networking and VPC Concepts at a practical level
topics.description: A subnet and its routes affect where traffic can go. A security group limits allowed flows for attached resources. The API can have an approved ingress path while its database only accepts the API's application traffic.

subtopics.title: AWS Networking and VPC Concepts at a practical level

topics.title: Object Storage with Amazon S3
topics.description: Object storage exposes objects by bucket and key. A workload often needs only a specific set of keys, not every object in the bucket. Keep access private and tie permissions to the actual workload and required actions.

topics.title: Managed PostgreSQL and secure database connectivity
topics.description: A managed database operates the database service, while the application still owns credentials, authorization and configuration. Use private connectivity where appropriate and verify the TLS peer identity instead of relying on encryption alone.

subtopics.title: Managed PostgreSQL and secure database connectivity

topics.title: Application Secrets, IAM Roles, and Least-Privilege Access
topics.description: A workload can receive temporary AWS credentials through a role and use them to request a secret by its resource identifier. Restrict both who can assume the role and what secret the role can access. Rotate the application credential separately from the workload credentials.

subtopics.title: Application Secrets, IAM Roles, and Least-Privilege Access

topics.title: Basic Cloud Logs, Health Monitoring, and Cost/Budget Awareness
topics.description: A healthy endpoint can still incur unexpected spend. Read service logs and health for runtime problems, then use cost budgets and tagged resources to review spending. Record storage and network resources that may outlive a stopped compute instance.

subtopics.title: Basic Cloud Logs, Health Monitoring, and Cost/Budget Awareness

topics.title: Secure Cloud Deployment Principles and Rollback Basics
topics.description: Before replacing a service, establish its health criteria and confirm the previous artifact still understands persisted data. A failed smoke test should trigger a rollback to a known artifact. Recheck both reachability and an authenticated request after restoration.

subtopics.title: Draw an AWS deployment with explicit access boundaries
Secure Cloud Deployment Principles and Rollback Basics

topics.title: Container Networking and Volumes in Multi-Service Environments
topics.description: Service discovery is scoped to networks. Publishing a port exposes a container listener through the host. Choose volumes independently from networks so a replaceable service can still use persistent data.

subtopics.title: Container Networking and Volumes in Multi-Service Environments

topics.title: Container Image Security and Minimal Images
topics.description: A multi-stage build can copy only the artifacts needed at runtime. Fewer packages reduce the material to inspect and maintain. Check the runtime user and report scanner findings in the context of the image's actual contents.

subtopics.title: Container Image Security and Minimal Images

topics.title: Release Strategies, Deployment Pipelines, and Rollbacks
topics.description: Promote a known artifact between environments. A staged rollout limits exposure while checking behavior. The previous build can only roll back safely if it still understands data and dependencies created during the rollout.

subtopics.title: Release Strategies, Deployment Pipelines, and Rollbacks

topics.title: Infrastructure as Code Fundamentals
topics.description: Infrastructure as code records intended resources as versioned definitions. Comparing intended and observed state can expose drift before applying a reviewed change.

topics.title: Terraform Fundamentals, State, and Safe Change Planning
topics.description: Terraform compares configuration with state and provider observations to prepare a plan. State can include sensitive metadata. A replacement can destroy a resource, so review its order, data implications and recovery before applying.

subtopics.title: Terraform Fundamentals, State, and Safe Change Planning

topics.title: Kubernetes Architecture and Core Concepts
topics.description: Kubernetes accepts desired state through its API and controllers work to reconcile it. The scheduler chooses nodes for pods. Node agents supervise execution on those nodes.

topics.title: Pods, Deployments, and Services
topics.description: A pod groups containers that share execution context. A Deployment reconciles replica state. A Service selects suitable pods and provides a stable network target while individual pod identities change.

topics.title: ConfigMaps, Secrets, and Configuration Injection
topics.description: ConfigMaps hold non-sensitive configuration. Secret objects can supply sensitive values, but access and storage protection still need configuration. How the app sees changes depends on the injection mechanism and its reload behavior.

topics.title: Readiness, Liveness, and Startup Probes
topics.description: Startup probes can protect slow initialisation. Readiness controls eligibility for traffic. Liveness can trigger a restart, so its check should reflect a failure a restart can plausibly fix.

topics.title: Resource Requests, Limits, and Horizontal Autoscaling
topics.description: Requests affect scheduling and can serve as a utilization baseline. Limits constrain resource consumption. Autoscaling adds replicas based on a signal, so it may react too late for an immediate burst.

subtopics.title: Resource Requests, Limits, and Horizontal Autoscaling

topics.title: Rolling Updates, Rollbacks, and Deploying a Small Service
topics.description: A rolling update replaces pods under configured availability and surge limits. Probe outcomes help decide whether replacement pods can serve traffic. A rollback restores the deployment specification and still needs compatibility verification.

subtopics.title: Rolling Updates, Rollbacks, and Deploying a Small Service

topics.title: MLOps Concepts and the ML Lifecycle
topics.description: MLOps connects model development to operational delivery. A training result is linked to a dataset and run. Promote a known artifact through checks and collect production evidence that can guide future work.

subtopics.title: MLOps Concepts and the ML Lifecycle

topics.title: Experiment Tracking with MLflow
topics.description: An MLflow run associates parameters, metrics and artifacts with an experiment. Two scores are comparable only when their data and metric contracts are compatible. Log those identities alongside the numbers.

topics.title: Model and Dataset Versioning Concepts
topics.description: An artifact version identifies a model output. A dataset version identifies the input used to train or evaluate it. Store the relationship explicitly so the model's evidence remains traceable.

topics.title: Model Registry and Promotion Workflow
topics.description: A registry helps identify available model versions and their lineage. A deployment chooses a version to serve. Keeping those actions separate lets reviewers compare evidence before changing runtime behavior.

topics.title: Reproducible Model Training and Evaluation
topics.description: A reproducible run records dataset identity, code, environment and split or seed information. Compare a metric and a few predictions to catch changes that an aggregate score can hide.

topics.title: Packaging and Deploying an ML Model
topics.description: Model packaging connects the artifact, expected input schema and runtime dependencies. A service must load the intended version and verify request shape before invoking the model.

subtopics.title: Packaging and Deploying an ML Model

topics.title: Basic Model Monitoring and Data/Prediction Quality Signals
topics.description: Input drift means observed features changed. Model performance requires appropriate outcomes or another quality signal to evaluate. Use changes as investigation triggers with clear baselines.

subtopics.title: Basic Model Monitoring and Data/Prediction Quality Signals

topics.title: LLM Application Configuration and Prompt Versioning
topics.description: A prompt is part of application behavior. Version the template alongside model selection and runtime parameters. A deployment record should say exactly which version produced a tested response.

subtopics.title: LLM Application Configuration and Prompt Versioning

topics.title: LLM Evaluation Pipelines and Regression Checks in CI
topics.description: A regression suite compares changed application behavior against known cases. Deterministic tests can run on every change. Live model evaluations may vary and need controlled inputs, costs and interpretation.

subtopics.title: LLM Evaluation Pipelines and Regression Checks in CI

topics.title: Provider, Latency, Token, and Cost Monitoring
topics.description: A single client request can involve several provider attempts. Record each attempt and aggregate them under a shared request identity. Separate timing and usage accounting from any confidential prompt text.

subtopics.title: Provider, Latency, Token, and Cost Monitoring

topics.title: AI Quality Monitoring and Feedback Signals
topics.description: User feedback can be valuable but may come from a changing subset of users. Use a repeatable review sample and a clearly defined metric before treating a feedback change as proof of a model regression.

subtopics.title: AI Quality Monitoring and Feedback Signals

topics.title: Safe Model, Prompt, and Application Rollbacks
topics.description: LLM behavior can change when the app, prompt or model changes independently. Rollback should restore a known compatible combination. Re-run an acceptance case after restoration.

subtopics.title: Safe Model, Prompt, and Application Rollbacks

topics.title: Continuous Training and Automated Retraining Architecture (advanced concepts; do not require the learner to build a large enterprise retraining platform)
topics.description: A retraining trigger starts an experiment. It does not establish that a new artifact is better. Review data and evaluation evidence before changing what serves requests.

subtopics.title: Continuous Training and Automated Retraining Architecture (advanced concepts; do not require the learner to build a large enterprise retraining platform)

topics.title: Structured Logging and Useful Log Context
topics.description: A structured log makes specific fields queryable. Request identity and failure category support diagnosis. Field policy and redaction protect private data even during errors.

subtopics.title: Structured Logging and Useful Log Context

topics.title: Metrics and Service Instrumentation
topics.description: Counters accumulate events and histograms summarize observations such as duration. Metric labels multiply time series, so choose bounded dimensions such as operation and outcome.

topics.title: Distributed Tracing and Request Correlation
topics.description: Distributed tracing links spans from separate processes through propagated context. Use timing and error fields to locate a slow or failing boundary. Keep sensitive data out of span attributes.

topics.title: OpenTelemetry Fundamentals
topics.description: A trace connects spans from one request. Metrics aggregate behavior across requests, while logs retain diagnostic events. A metric label for each individual request or account creates unbounded series.

subtopics.title: Trace a failed model request and count it safely

topics.title: Prometheus Metrics and Basic Instrumentation
topics.description: Prometheus can scrape exposed service metrics at intervals. A counter rate estimates change over time and handles restarts according to the query semantics. Confirm the target is being scraped before diagnosing the application.

topics.title: Grafana Dashboards and Alerts
topics.description: A Grafana panel queries a data source over a time range. An alert evaluates a condition over one or more windows. Test how it behaves when measurements are missing as well as when the threshold is exceeded.

topics.title: Error Monitoring and Incident Signals
topics.description: Grouping similar errors can expose recurrence, while release labels help associate a new class with a change. Include counts, denominators and affected versions before deciding whether to alert.

topics.title: OWASP API Security Risks
topics.description: An API can be reachable to an authenticated user while its object ownership checks are wrong. Validate scope, bound resource use and treat upstream destinations and response data as part of the threat model.

topics.title: Authentication, Authorization, RBAC, and Tenant Isolation Review
topics.description: Authentication establishes identity. Authorization applies the action and resource policy. A privileged role in one tenant does not automatically establish authority over another tenant's resources.

subtopics.title: Authentication, Authorization, RBAC, and Tenant Isolation Review

topics.title: PII Protection, Redaction, and Data Privacy
topics.description: Collect fields needed for the stated purpose and document where they can persist. Redact sensitive values before diagnostics are emitted. Deletion and retention policies should account for derived copies as well as original records.

subtopics.title: Awareness of applicable privacy and compliance requirements
PII Protection, Redaction, and Data Privacy

topics.title: Encryption in Transit and at Rest
topics.description: Transport encryption protects traffic and peer verification authenticates the endpoint. Storage encryption protects data under different access assumptions. Review who can read plaintext and who can use the relevant key.

subtopics.title: Encryption in Transit and at Rest

topics.title: Database Security, Backups, and Restore Verification
topics.description: A backup is only useful when it can be restored. Restore into an isolated environment, verify data and permissions and measure the time and recovery point against the service's objectives.

subtopics.title: Database Security, Backups, and Restore Verification

topics.title: Dependency and Software Supply-Chain Security
topics.description: A dependency can enter through another package. Inspect the resolved dependency graph before choosing a fix. Record the affected versions, and verify the change against real application behavior.

topics.title: AI-Specific Security Threats and Tool Permission Boundaries
topics.description: Text from a model or retrieved source is untrusted data. Validate tool arguments and check authorization outside the model. Require explicit approval for sensitive actions under the service's policy.

subtopics.title: AI-Specific Security Threats and Tool Permission Boundaries

topics.title: Incident Response and Operational Runbooks
topics.description: A runbook describes a safe response to a known symptom. Record what was observed and which intervention changed behavior. Separate mitigation during the incident from later investigation.

topics.title: Load Testing with Locust
topics.description: Load testing applies controlled traffic to measure a system under expected and exceptional demand. Percentiles reveal slow requests that averages conceal.

subtopics.title: Measure an AI API workload with Locust

topics.title: Stress Testing and Bottleneck Analysis
topics.description: A stress test deliberately crosses a service limit. Watch for the first resource that saturates and check recovery after load falls. A high error rate without resource evidence does not establish the cause.

topics.title: Production Readiness Review and Rollback Verification
topics.description: A readiness review links requirements to measured behavior, operational ownership and a recovery path. A rollback is an observed result only after the previous version serves the expected contract under the current data state.

subtopics.title: Production Readiness Review and Rollback Verification

title: Model Serving, GPU Infrastructure, and Inference Optimization
purpose: Measure throughput, latency, memory and cost when operating a model endpoint with vLLM.
why: Measure throughput, latency, memory and cost when operating a model endpoint with vLLM.
outcomes: Publish a reproducible benchmark with capacity and cost estimates tied to an explicit workload.
A reader can rerun the comparison and reproduce metric and cost calculations within a stated tolerance.

topics.title: Model Serving Fundamentals and When Self-Hosting Is Necessary
topics.description: A serving process loads model weights once, validates incoming requests and schedules inference work. It also needs readiness checks before it accepts traffic. Diagram model loading, readiness, request validation and prediction. Specify a health response before and after the model loads.

topics.title: Hosted API vs Self-Hosted Model: Cost, Control, Latency, and Operational Trade-Offs
topics.description: A hosted API can charge by token while an owned runtime consumes capacity even when idle. Compare the same request distribution and service target. Data retention, network latency, model control, incident response and operator time can change the decision before a raw cost break-even point.

subtopics.title: Hosted API vs Self-Hosted Model: Cost, Control, Latency, and Operational Trade-Offs

topics.title: Inference Architecture and Request Lifecycle
topics.description: A synchronous request waits for a response. A batch job can record a request and produce results later with a separate status check. Draw the two lifecycles and mark when the client learns about failure. State which lifecycle fits a million offline predictions.

subtopics.title: Inference Architecture and Request Lifecycle · worked exercise

topics.title: CPU and GPU Execution Differences
topics.description: A GPU can execute many similar operations concurrently. A tiny job may still take longer if data transfer and launch overhead outweigh its parallel work. Compare a small and a large matrix operation conceptually. List the computation and data transfers a fair benchmark would measure.

subtopics.title: CPU and GPU Execution Differences · worked exercise

topics.title: GPU Architecture Fundamentals
topics.description: A GPU groups many execution units and runs large numbers of concurrent threads. Work must expose parallel operations to keep them busy. Sketch independent element-wise work and a sequential dependency chain. Identify which offers more parallel work and where synchronization is needed.

topics.title: CUDA Concepts and the GPU Software Stack (conceptual and practical usage level; do not require kernel programming)
topics.description: An application, GPU runtime and device driver cooperate to execute kernels. A model can fail before inference if the installed components do not support the device. Record the hardware and software versions for an owned environment or an example configuration. Make a version compatibility checklist and a test for GPU visibility.

subtopics.title: CUDA Concepts and GPU Software Stack · worked exercise

topics.title: GPU Memory, VRAM, and Memory Bandwidth
topics.description: Capacity measures bytes that can fit. Bandwidth measures bytes transferred per unit time. Both can limit a model in different ways. Calculate how long it would take to read 16 GB at 800 GB/s under idealized assumptions. Separately check whether the bytes fit on a 12 GB device.

subtopics.title: GPU Memory, VRAM, and Memory Bandwidth · worked exercise

topics.title: Loading Model Weights and Runtime Memory Requirements
topics.description: One billion weights at two bytes each take about two gigabytes before additional runtime memory. Inference also uses activations and cache. Estimate weight bytes for two parameter counts and build a memory budget including a separate runtime reserve. State what remains unmeasured.

subtopics.title: Loading Model Weights and Runtime Memory · worked exercise

topics.title: Quantization and Precision Trade-Offs
topics.description: Lower precision can reduce weight storage and memory traffic, while rounding can change model quality. Performance depends on available kernels and workload. Compute the idealized weight ratio for 16-bit and 8-bit weights. Design a comparison using the same prompts and a quality measure.

subtopics.title: Quantization and Precision Trade-Offs · worked exercise

topics.title: Batching and Dynamic Batching
topics.description: Combining requests can improve device utilization. Waiting to form a batch can add latency for an individual request. Trace three requests arriving at different times under an immediate and a short batch wait policy. Compare wait and number of launches.

subtopics.title: Batching and Dynamic Batching · worked exercise

topics.title: Prefill and Decode Stages
topics.description: Prefill processes prompt tokens. Autoregressive decode uses the prior context and produces further tokens step by step. Draw a request with a five-token prompt and three output tokens. Identify the work contributing to first-token time and subsequent intervals.

subtopics.title: Prefill and Decode Stages · worked exercise

topics.title: KV Cache Fundamentals
topics.description: The KV cache retains attention keys and values from earlier positions. Longer active sequences require more cache space. For a simplified fixed cache cost of 10 KB per token, calculate memory for two sequences of different lengths. Add a third sequence and check the budget.

topics.title: Inference Throughput, Latency, and Tokens per Second
topics.description: Throughput measures work completed per time. Latency measures time for one request. High aggregate throughput can coexist with high request latency. Compare two measured toy runs with different request counts, elapsed times and p95 values. State which objective each run better meets.

subtopics.title: Inference Throughput and Latency · worked exercise

topics.title: Concurrent Request Capacity and Queueing
topics.description: Output tokens per second combines work across active requests. The number of simultaneous requests sustainable at an SLO also depends on length and latency. Given 300 output tokens in 10 seconds, compute throughput. Explain what extra observations are needed to infer a safe concurrent user limit.

subtopics.title: Tokens per Second and Concurrent Request Capacity · worked exercise

topics.title: Memory Optimization Fundamentals
topics.description: Reducing maximum input length can shrink the worst-case cache demand. It changes which user requests can be accepted. Design a memory guard with a maximum context and concurrency budget. Test a boundary request and record the rejection reason.

topics.title: Model Parallelism Concepts
topics.description: Sharding a model across devices distributes weights and work. Moving intermediate data between devices adds communication cost. Diagram one model split across two devices. Mark the messages needed for one inference step and identify a bottleneck if communication is slow.

topics.title: Distributed Inference Fundamentals (architecture overview before any cluster-level implementation)
topics.description: Replicas process independent requests. A sharded model may need several devices to work on the same request. Draw a two-replica deployment and a two-device shard. For each, show what happens when one device becomes unavailable.

topics.title: vLLM Fundamentals and Architecture
topics.description: vLLM schedules requests and manages inference memory. Serving behavior depends on model size, workload and configuration. Use the official quickstart to plan a local run. Record the model, vLLM version, device and context limit, then validate an owned health or inference response if hardware is available.

subtopics.title: vLLM Fundamentals and Architecture · worked exercise

topics.title: OpenAI-Compatible Model Serving APIs
topics.description: A compatible endpoint exposes a familiar request shape, but supported fields and behavior can depend on the server and model. Write a contract test for a known model and a malformed request against a local stub. Document which response fields the client relies on.

subtopics.title: OpenAI-Compatible Model Serving APIs · worked exercise

topics.title: Serving a Model Behind a FastAPI Backend
topics.description: An application gateway can authenticate, enforce quotas and bound time before forwarding a request to a private model server. Draw the caller, gateway and private serving boundary. Specify the response for denial, model unavailability and a timeout.

subtopics.title: Serving Models Behind a Backend API · worked exercise

topics.title: GPU Utilization and Runtime Monitoring
topics.description: High memory usage does not necessarily mean all GPU compute units are busy. Interpret utilization with queue depth, model latency and workload. Design a dashboard with memory, utilization, queue depth and first-token latency. Explain what evidence would identify memory pressure.

subtopics.title: GPU Utilization and Runtime Monitoring · worked exercise

topics.title: Profiling and Bottleneck Analysis
topics.description: A bottleneck hypothesis should predict which measurement changes when a single workload variable changes. Compare one prompt-length change at fixed concurrency and output length. Identify what results would favor a prefill bottleneck.

subtopics.title: Profiling and Bottleneck Analysis · worked exercise

topics.title: Inference Optimization Techniques
topics.description: Optimization is a trade-off. Increasing batching can raise throughput and make the latency tail worse for interactive requests. Define a baseline and change one scheduling setting. Report p95 and throughput on the same workload or describe the measurements still needed.

topics.title: Autoscaling and Model Server Capacity
topics.description: Model replicas may take time to load weights. A scaling policy based only on average CPU can miss the waiting requests. Design a policy using queue depth and measured readiness delay. Draw a burst and mark when new capacity can become useful.

subtopics.title: Autoscaling and Model Server Capacity · worked exercise

topics.title: Inference Reliability, Timeouts, and Recovery
topics.description: A timeout protects the caller's deadline, but server work may continue unless cancellation reaches it. Retrying blindly can double the load. Inject one slow stub response. Track the caller deadline and cancellation, then verify retries are bounded by remaining time.

subtopics.title: Inference Reliability, Timeouts, and Recovery · worked exercise

topics.title: Performance and Cost Benchmarking
topics.description: A useful report states workload, hardware, model and output limits. Compare cost per useful result alongside throughput and quality. Create a reproducible benchmark comparing two prompt lengths. Report actual time-to-first-token and output throughput only for executed runs.

subtopics.title: Benchmark prefill and decoding under a controlled load

title: Portfolio Engineering and CCAI Production Capstone
purpose: Integrate the portfolio services into CCAI, then demonstrate reliability and capacity with recorded evidence.
why: Integrate the portfolio services into CCAI, then demonstrate reliability and capacity with recorded evidence.
outcomes: Trace a request through the routing policy.
Produce repeatable evidence for failure handling and capacity.

topics.title: CCAI integration and operational evidence
topics.description: Integrate the preceding API, model, retrieval and orchestration work. Prove routing, tenant isolation and recovery with repeatable tests and recorded measurements.

subtopics.title: Prove CCAI routing, isolation and recovery
